70:         return True
71:     if len(t) < 12:
72:         return False
73:     if t[-1] not in ".!?":
74:         return False
75:     if t[0].islower():
76:         return False
77:     if "  " in t:
78:         return False
79:     words = t.split()
80:     if any(a == b for a, b in itertools.pairwise(words)):
81:         return False
82:     # No long all-caps run (e.g. an uncorrected acronym sequence like "API API").
83:     return not any(len(w) >= 5 and w.isupper() for w in words)
84: 
85: 
86: class Session:
87:     """One active translation session bound to a single WebSocket connection."""
88: 
89:     def __init__(self, session_id: str, websocket: WebSocket, settings: Settings) -> None:
90:         self.session_id = session_id
91:         self.websocket = websocket
92:         self.settings = settings
93:         self.config: schemas.SessionConfiguration | None = None
94:         self.state = "created"
95:         self.received_chunks = 0
96:         self.received_bytes = 0
97:         self.audio_seconds = 0.0
98:         self.last_audio_at = 0.0
99:         self.last_ack_at = 0.0
100:         self.bytes_per_second = 32000.0
101:         self.last_vad_event: schemas.VADEventMessage | None = None
102:         self.speech_started_at_ms: int | None = None
103:         self.asr: ASRProvider | None = None
104:         self.asr_task: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None
105:         self.silence_detector: SilenceDetector | None = None
106:         self.translator: TranslationProvider | None = None
107:         self.translation_queue: (
108:             asyncio.Queue[tuple[str, str, float | None]] | None
109:         ) = None
110:         self.translation_task: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None
111:         # Async LLM refinement: a separate, non-blocking worker that corrects
112:         # finalized segments after the live caption/translation already
113:         # reached the client. Never awaited on the hot path.
114:         self.refiner: LLMProvider | None = None
115:         self.refinement_queue: (
116:             asyncio.Queue[tuple[str, str, str, list[str]]] | None
117:         ) = None
118:         self.refinement_task: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None
119:         self.context_window: list[str] = []
120:         self.refinement_context_size = 4
121:         self._send_lock = asyncio.Lock()
122: 
123:     @property
124:     def configured(self) -> bool:
125:         return self.config is not None
126: 
127:     async def apply_config(self, config: schemas.SessionConfiguration) -> None:
128:         self.config = config
129:         self.state = "configured"
130:         self.bytes_per_second = self._bytes_per_second(config)
131:         self.silence_detector = SilenceDetector(
132:             finalize_ms=self.settings.silence_finalize_ms,
133:             min_speech_ms=self.settings.silence_min_speech_ms,
134:         )
135:         await self._teardown_providers()
136:         self.asr = create_asr_provider()
137:         self.asr_task = asyncio.create_task(
138:             self._run_asr(), name=f"asr-{self.session_id}"
139:         )
140:         self.translator = create_translation_provider()
141:         self.translation_queue = asyncio.Queue()
142:         self.translation_task = asyncio.create_task(
143:             self._run_translation(), name=f"translation-{self.session_id}"
144:         )
145: 
146:         self.refinement_context_size = max(0, self.settings.llm_context_segments)
147:         self.context_window = []
148:         self.refiner = create_llm_provider()
149:         if self.refiner is not None:
150:             self.refinement_queue = asyncio.Queue()
151:             self.refinement_task = asyncio.create_task(
152:                 self._run_refinement(), name=f"refinement-{self.session_id}"
153:             )
154:         else:
155:             self.refinement_queue = None
156:             self.refinement_task = None
157: 
158:     async def _teardown_providers(self) -> None:
159:         """Cancel/close any providers from a previous configuration (defensive)."""
160:         for task in (self.asr_task, self.translation_task, self.refinement_task):
161:             if task is not None and not task.done() and task is not asyncio.current_task():
162:                 task.cancel()
163:                 try:
164:                     await task
165:                 except (asyncio.CancelledError, Exception):
166:                     logger.debug("provider_task_cancel", session_id=self.session_id)
167:         for provider in (self.asr, self.translator, self.refiner):
168:             if provider is not None:
169:                 try:
170:                     await provider.close()
171:                 except Exception:
172:                     logger.debug("provider_close_failed", session_id=self.session_id)
173:         self.asr = None
174:         self.asr_task = None
175:         self.translator = None
176:         self.translation_queue = None
177:         self.translation_task = None
178:         self.refiner = None
179:         self.refinement_queue = None
180:         self.refinement_task = None
181:         self.context_window = []
182: 
183:     async def receive_audio(self, chunk: bytes) -> None:
184:         if not self.configured:
185:             await self._send_error("no_active_session", "Configure a session before sending audio")
186:             return
187:         now = time.monotonic()
188:         self.received_chunks += 1
189:         self.received_bytes += len(chunk)
190:         self.audio_seconds += len(chunk) / self.bytes_per_second
191:         self.last_audio_at = now
192: 
193:         if self.asr is not None:
194:             await self.asr.send_audio(chunk)
195: 
196:         if now - self.last_ack_at >= _AUDIO_ACK_INTERVAL_MS / 1000:
197:             self.last_ack_at = now
198:             await self.send_event(
199:                 schemas.AudioReceivedEvent(
200:                     session_id=self.session_id,
201:                     chunks=self.received_chunks,
202:                     bytes=self.received_bytes,
203:                     audio_seconds=round(self.audio_seconds, 3),
204:                 )
205:             )
206:             logger.info(
207:                 "audio_received",
208:                 session_id=self.session_id,
209:                 chunks=self.received_chunks,
210:                 bytes=self.received_bytes,
211:                 audio_seconds=round(self.audio_seconds, 3),
212:             )
213: 
214:     async def stop(self, reason: str) -> None:
215:         if self.state == "stopped":
216:             return
217:         self.state = "stopped"
218:         current = asyncio.current_task()
219:         for attr in ("asr_task", "translation_task", "refinement_task"):
220:             task = getattr(self, attr)
221:             setattr(self, attr, None)
222:             if task is not None and not task.done() and task is not current:
223:                 task.cancel()
224:                 try:
225:                     await task
226:                 except (asyncio.CancelledError, Exception):
227:                     logger.debug("session_task_cancel", session_id=self.session_id)
228:         for attr, provider in (
229:             ("asr", self.asr),
230:             ("translator", self.translator),
231:             ("refiner", self.refiner),
232:         ):
233:             setattr(self, attr, None)
234:             if provider is not None:
235:                 try:
236:                     await provider.close()
237:                 except Exception:
238:                     logger.debug("provider_close_failed", session_id=self.session_id)
239:         await self.send_event(
240:             schemas.SessionStoppedEvent(session_id=self.session_id, reason=reason)
241:         )
242: 
243:     async def _run_asr(self) -> None:
244:         """Connect the ASR provider and stream transcript events to the client."""
245:         config = self.config
246:         if config is None or self.asr is None:
247:             return
248:         try:
249:             await self.asr.connect(
250:                 sample_rate=config.sample_rate,
251:                 encoding=config.encoding,
252:                 language=config.source_language,
253:             )
254:         except ASRProviderError as exc:
255:             await self.send_event(
256:                 schemas.ErrorMessage(
257:                     session_id=self.session_id, code=exc.code, message=exc.message
258:                 )
259:             )
260:             await self.stop(reason="asr_error")
261:             return
262: 
263:         try:
264:             async for segment in self.asr.stream():
265:                 await self.send_event(
266:                     schemas.TranscriptEvent(
267:                         type="final_transcript" if segment.is_final else "partial_transcript",
268:                         session_id=self.session_id,
269:                         segment_id=segment.segment_id,
270:                         text=segment.text,
271:                         is_final=segment.is_final,
272:                         start_ms=segment.start_ms,
273:                         end_ms=segment.end_ms,
274:                         confidence=segment.confidence,
275:                     )
276:                 )
277:                 if segment.asr_latency_ms is not None:
278:                     # asr_latency_ms is T2 (content received) -> result emitted.
279:                     latency = round(segment.asr_latency_ms, 1)
280:                     if segment.is_final:
281:                         await self.send_event(
282:                             schemas.LatencyEvent(
283:                                 session_id=self.session_id,
284:                                 segment_id=segment.segment_id,
285:                                 asr_ms=latency,
286:                                 asr_final_ms=latency,
287:                             )
288:                         )
289:                     else:
290:                         await self.send_event(
291:                             schemas.LatencyEvent(
292:                                 session_id=self.session_id,
293:                                 segment_id=segment.segment_id,
294:                                 asr_ms=latency,
295:                                 asr_partial_ms=latency,
296:                             )
297:                         )
298:                 # Only finalized, meaningful utterances are translated --
299:                 # partials stream straight to the client and never enqueue.
300:                 # The ASR final latency is threaded through so the translation
301:                 # latency report can carry a true server-side end-to-end figure.
302:                 if segment.is_final and self.translation_queue is not None:
303:                     self.translation_queue.put_nowait(
304:                         (
305:                             segment.segment_id,
306:                             segment.text,
307:                             segment.asr_latency_ms,
308:                         )
309:                     )
310: 
311:                 # Async LLM refinement: enqueue right after finalization, but
312:                 # NEVER await the result before the final transcript/translation
313:                 # events have already been sent above. A rolling window of prior
314:                 # finalized segments is captured as context.
315:                 if (
316:                     segment.is_final
317:                     and self.refinement_queue is not None
318:                     and self.refiner is not None
319:                 ):
320:                     context = list(self.context_window)
321:                     self.refinement_queue.put_nowait(
322:                         (segment.segment_id, segment.text, config.source_language, context)
323:                     )
324:                     self.context_window.append(segment.text)
325:                     if len(self.context_window) > self.refinement_context_size:
326:                         self.context_window = self.context_window[-self.refinement_context_size:]
327:         except asyncio.CancelledError:
328:             pass
329:         except ASRProviderError as exc:
330:             await self.send_event(
331:                 schemas.ErrorMessage(
332:                     session_id=self.session_id, code=exc.code, message=exc.message
333:                 )
334:             )
335:             await self.stop(reason="asr_error")
336:         finally:
337:             asr = self.asr
338:             if asr is not None:
339:                 try:
340:                     await asr.close()
341:                 except Exception:
342:                     logger.debug("asr_close_failed", session_id=self.session_id)
343: 
344:     async def _run_translation(self) -> None:
345:         """Translate finalized utterances in order and stream results to the client.
346: 
347:         A single queue + worker per session keeps translation results in
348:         utterance order. A translation failure is non-fatal: the error is
349:         reported but the session (and all later utterances) keep going.
350:         """
351:         config = self.config
352:         translator = self.translator
353:         queue = self.translation_queue
354:         if config is None or translator is None or queue is None:
355:             return
356:         while True:
357:             segment_id, text, asr_final_ms = await queue.get()
358:             started = time.monotonic()
359:             try:
360:                 result = await translator.translate(
361:                     segment_id=segment_id,
362:                     text=text,
363:                     source_language=config.source_language,
364:                     target_language=config.target_language,
365:                     is_final=True,
366:                 )
367:             except asyncio.CancelledError:
368:                 raise
369:             except TranslationError as exc:
370:                 logger.warning(
371:                     "translation_failed",
372:                     session_id=self.session_id,
373:                     code=exc.code,
374:                     message=exc.message,
375:                 )
376:                 await self.send_event(
377:                     schemas.ErrorMessage(
378:                         session_id=self.session_id,
379:                         code="translation_failed",
380:                         message=exc.message,
381:                     )
382:                 )
383:                 continue
384:             except Exception as exc:
385:                 logger.warning(
386:                     "translation_failed",
387:                     session_id=self.session_id,
388:                     error=str(exc),
389:                 )
390:                 await self.send_event(
391:                     schemas.ErrorMessage(
392:                         session_id=self.session_id,
393:                         code="translation_failed",
394:                         message=str(exc),
395:                     )
396:                 )
397:                 continue
398: 
399:             translation_ms = round((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000, 1)
400:             # Server-side live-path end-to-end: T2 -> T6. ASR final latency
401:             # ends at T4 and translation begins immediately after (T5 ~ T4),
402:             # so end_to_end = asr_final + translation. Refinement is excluded.
403:             end_to_end_ms = (
404:                 round(asr_final_ms + translation_ms, 1)
405:                 if asr_final_ms is not None
406:                 else None
407:             )
408:             await self.send_event(
409:                 schemas.TranslationEvent(
410:                     session_id=self.session_id,
411:                     segment_id=result.segment_id,
412:                     source_text=result.source_text,
413:                     translated_text=result.translated_text,
414:                     source_language=result.source_language,
415:                     target_language=result.target_language,
416:                     is_final=result.is_final,
417:                     provider=result.provider,
418:                 )
419:             )
420:             await self.send_event(
421:                 schemas.LatencyEvent(
422:                     session_id=self.session_id,
423:                     segment_id=result.segment_id,
424:                     asr_final_ms=round(asr_final_ms, 1)
425:                     if asr_final_ms is not None
426:                     else None,
427:                     translation_ms=translation_ms,
428:                     end_to_end_ms=end_to_end_ms,
429:                 )
430:             )
431: 
432:     async def _run_refinement(self) -> None:
433:         """Correct finalized segments in the background, never blocking anything.
434: 
435:         Runs as its own task with its own queue, fully independent of the ASR
436:         and translation tasks. A failure (timeout, API error, invalid output)
437:         is logged and the original transcript/translation is kept as-is -- the
438:         live captioning path never notices.
439:         """
440:         queue = self.refinement_queue
441:         refiner = self.refiner
442:         if queue is None or refiner is None:
443:             return
444:         while True:
445:             segment_id, text, language, context = await queue.get()
446:             if self.settings.llm_skip_when_clean and _looks_clean(text):
447:                 logger.debug(
448:                     "refinement_skipped_clean",
449:                     session_id=self.session_id,
450:                     segment_id=segment_id,
451:                 )
452:                 continue
453:             started = time.monotonic()
454:             result = None
455:             try:
456:                 result = await refiner.refine(
457:                     segment_id=segment_id,
458:                     text=text,
459:                     language=language,
460:                     context=context,
461:                 )
462:             except asyncio.CancelledError:
463:                 raise
464:             except Exception as exc:
465:                 logger.warning(
466:                     "refinement_failed",
467:                     session_id=self.session_id,
468:                     segment_id=segment_id,
469:                     error=str(exc),
470:                 )
471:             finally:
472:                 # Refinement latency is reported separately from the live path,
473:                 # even when the attempt itself failed.
474:                 refinement_ms = round((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000, 1)
475:                 await self.send_event(
476:                     schemas.LatencyEvent(
477:                         session_id=self.session_id,
478:                         segment_id=segment_id,
479:                         refinement_ms=refinement_ms,
480:                     )
481:                 )
482:             if result is not None and result.changed:
483:                 await self.send_event(
484:                     schemas.RefinedTranscriptEvent(
485:                         session_id=self.session_id,
486:                         segment_id=segment_id,
487:                         refined_text=result.refined_text,
488:                         changed=True,
489:                     )
490:                 )
491: 
492:     async def send_event(self, event: schemas.ServerEvent) -> None:
493:         async with self._send_lock:
494:             try:
495:                 # Serialize once to JSON-safe primitives (compact, like the
496:                 # built-in send_json); audio stays binary on the wire.
497:                 text = json.dumps(
498:                     event.model_dump(mode="json"), separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False
499:                 )
500:                 await self.websocket.send_text(text)
501:             except Exception:
502:                 logger.debug("ws_send_failed", session_id=self.session_id, event_type=event.type)
503: 
504:     async def _send_error(self, code: str, message: str) -> None:
505:         await self.send_event(
506:             schemas.ErrorMessage(
507:                 session_id=self.session_id,
508:                 code=code,
509:                 message=message,
510:             )
511:         )
512: 
513:     @staticmethod
514:     def _bytes_per_second(config: schemas.SessionConfiguration) -> float:
515:         factor = _AUDIO_BYTES_PER_SECOND_BY_ENCODING.get(config.encoding, 2)
516:         return max(1.0, float(config.sample_rate) * factor)
517: 
518: 
519: class SessionManager:
520:     """Registry of live sessions keyed by session id."""
521: 
522:     def __init__(self) -> None:
523:         self._sessions: dict[str, Session] = {}
524: 
525:     def create(self, websocket: WebSocket, session_id: str) -> Session:
526:         session = Session(session_id, websocket, get_settings())
527:         self._sessions[session_id] = session
528:         return session
529: 
530:     def get(self, session_id: str) -> Session | None:
531:         return self._sessions.get(session_id)
532: 
533:     def remove(self, session_id: str) -> Session | None:
534:         return self._sessions.pop(session_id, None)
535: 
536: 
537: session_manager = SessionManager()
538: 
539: 
540: async def _send_error(websocket: WebSocket, code: str, message: str) -> None:
541:     try:
542:         await websocket.send_json(
543:             schemas.ErrorMessage(code=code, message=message).model_dump()
544:         )
545:     except Exception:
546:         logger.debug("ws_send_error_ignored", code=code)
547: 
548: 
549: async def _handle_start_session(
550:     websocket: WebSocket,
551:     payload: dict,
552:     current: Session | None,
553: ) -> Session | None:
554:     try:
555:         request = schemas.StartSessionRequest.model_validate(payload)
556:     except ValidationError as exc:
557:         await _send_error(websocket, "invalid_message", f"Invalid start_session: {exc}")
558:         return current
559: 
560:     if current is not None:
561:         await _send_error(
562:             websocket, "session_already_active", "A session is already active on this connection"
563:         )
564:         return current
565: 
566:     session_id = request.session_id or uuid.uuid4().hex
567:     if session_manager.get(session_id) is not None:
568:         await _send_error(websocket, "session_exists", f"Session {session_id} already exists")
569:         return current
570: 
571:     session = session_manager.create(websocket, session_id)
572:     logger.info("session_created", session_id=session_id, waiting_for_config=True)
573:     return session
574: 
575: 
576: async def _handle_configuration(
577:     websocket: WebSocket,
578:     payload: dict,
579:     current: Session | None,
580: ) -> Session | None:
581:     try:
582:         config = schemas.SessionConfiguration.model_validate(payload)
583:     except ValidationError as exc:
584:         await _send_error(websocket, "invalid_message", f"Invalid session_configuration: {exc}")
585:         return current
586: 
587:     session = session_manager.get(config.session_id)
588:     if session is None:
589:         session = session_manager.create(websocket, config.session_id)
590:     elif session.websocket is not websocket:
591:         await _send_error(
592:             websocket,
593:             "session_in_use",
594:             f"Session {config.session_id} belongs to another connection",
595:         )
596:         return current
597: 
598:     if current is not None and current is not session:
599:         await _send_error(
600:             websocket,
601:             "cannot_switch_sessions",
602:             "Cannot reconfigure a different session on this connection",
603:         )
604:         return current
605: 
606:     await session.apply_config(config)
607:     await session.send_event(
608:         schemas.SessionStartedEvent(
609:             session_id=session.session_id,
610:             configuration=config,
611:         )
612:     )
613:     logger.info(
614:         "session_configured",
615:         session_id=session.session_id,
616:         source_language=config.source_language,
617:         target_language=config.target_language,
618:         audio_source=config.audio_source,
619:     )
620:     return session
621: 
622: 
623: async def _handle_stop_session(
624:     websocket: WebSocket,
625:     payload: dict,
626:     current: Session | None,
627: ) -> Session | None:
628:     try:
629:         request = schemas.StopSessionRequest.model_validate(payload)
630:     except ValidationError as exc:
631:         await _send_error(websocket, "invalid_message", f"Invalid stop_session: {exc}")
632:         return current
633: 
634:     session = session_manager.get(request.session_id)
635:     if session is None or session.websocket is not websocket:
636:         await _send_error(websocket, "no_active_session", "No matching session on this connection")
637:         return current
638: 
639:     await session.stop(reason="client_request")
640:     session_manager.remove(request.session_id)
641:     logger.info("session_stopped", session_id=request.session_id)
642:     return None
643: 
644: 
645: async def _handle_audio_chunk_control(
646:     websocket: WebSocket,
647:     payload: dict,
648:     current: Session | None,
649: ) -> None:
650:     try:
651:         schemas.AudioChunkMessage.model_validate(payload)
652:     except ValidationError as exc:
653:         await _send_error(websocket, "invalid_message", f"Invalid audio_chunk: {exc}")
654:         return
655:     if current is None:
656:         await _send_error(websocket, "no_active_session", "No session on this connection")
657:         return
658:     logger.debug("audio_chunk_control", session_id=current.session_id)
659: 
660: 
661: async def _handle_vad_event(
662:     websocket: WebSocket,
663:     payload: dict,
664:     current: Session | None,
665: ) -> None:
666:     try:
667:         message = schemas.VADEventMessage.model_validate(payload)
668:     except ValidationError as exc:
669:         await _send_error(websocket, "invalid_message", f"Invalid vad_event: {exc}")
670:         return
671:     if current is None or current.session_id != message.session_id:
672:         await _send_error(websocket, "no_active_session", "No matching session on this connection")
673:         return
674: 
675:     if message.event == "speech_started":
676:         current.speech_started_at_ms = message.timestamp_ms
677: 
678:     # Stash the latest transition so utterance finalization can use the last
679:     # measured silence gap (duration_ms on silence_detected).
680:     current.last_vad_event = message
681:     logger.debug(
682:         "vad_event",
683:         session_id=message.session_id,
684:         vad_event=message.event,
685:         timestamp_ms=message.timestamp_ms,
686:         duration_ms=message.duration_ms,
687:     )
688: 
689:     # A client-detected silence boundary becomes an endpointing hint for the
690:     # ASR provider (Deepgram "Finalize"), but only when the gap is significant
691:     # enough per server-side SilenceDetector policy.
692:     if message.event == "silence_detected" and current.asr is not None:
693:         detector = current.silence_detector

## User

The app's default sourceLanguage is 'auto' (frontend/src/config/preferences.ts), but NLLBTranslationProvider rejects 'auto' by design (no offline language detection) and the default .env.example ships with no cloud translation API key. This means a fresh, unconfigured install has 100% translation failure by default with no clear signal why. Either change the default sourceLanguage to a concrete language code, or add a startup check in backend/app/main.py/create_translation_provider() that logs a clear one-time warning when neither cloud credentials nor a usable offline provider are configured

def warn_on_translation_misconfiguration(settings: Settings) -> None:
    """Log a clear one-time warning when translation is effectively unusable."""

    elif settings.translation_provider == "nllb" and not offline_available:
        logger.warning(...)
    elif settings.translation_provider == "hybrid" and not cloud_key_configured and not offline_available:
        logger.warning(...)

## User

I went through the codebase focusing on things that would actually break the app at runtime (not style nits). Here are the real bugs I found, in order of severity, each with a concrete fix.

1. (Critical) Every live session start sends duplicate start_session/session_configuration → spurious error on every "Start"

File: frontend/src/lib/wsClient.ts

In App.tsx, handleStart calls:

js
client.connect()
client.sendStartSession(session.session_id)
client.sendConfiguration(session)

These three calls are synchronous. connect() opens a WebSocket, but the socket is still CONNECTING when sendStartSession/sendConfiguration run, so both get pushed into this.pending.

Then TranslatorClient.openSocket()'s onopen handler unconditionally re-adds the same two messages:

js
socket.onopen = () => {
  this.reconnectAttempts = 0
  if (this.startSessionId) {
    this.pending.unshift({ type: "start_session", session_id: this.startSessionId })
  }
  if (this.configuration) {
    this.pending.push({ type: "session_configuration", ...this.configuration })
  }
  this.flushQueue()
  ...
}

Result: the backend receives start_session twice. The second one hits _handle_start_session's if current is not None: branch and returns a session_already_active error, which the frontend treats as fatal (setStatus("error")) immediately after every start. The duplicate session_configuration also re-runs apply_config, tearing down and recreating ASR/translation providers a second time (wasted Deepgram connections).

Fix — only synthesize the replay messages on onopen when nothing is already queued (i.e. this is a genuine reconnect, not the initial connect):

js
socket.onopen = () => {
  this.reconnectAttempts = 0
  if (this.pending.length === 0) {
    if (this.startSessionId) {
      this.pending.push({ type: "start_session", session_id: this.startSessionId })
    }
    if (this.configuration) {
      this.pending.push({ type: "session_configuration", ...this.configuration })
    }
  }
  this.flushQueue()
  this.setState("connected")
}

Prompt you can give: "In frontend/src/lib/wsClient.ts, TranslatorClient.openSocket()'s onopen handler unconditionally re-queues start_session and session_configuration, duplicating messages already queued by the initial synchronous sendStartSession/sendConfiguration calls before the socket opened. Change it to only synthesize those replay messages when this.pending.length === 0, so it only fires on real reconnects, not on the first connect."

2. (Critical) "Demo (no backend)" mode does nothing

File: frontend/src/providers/streaming/mockStreamingClient.ts

MockStreamingClient only ever emits a session_started event. sendAudio and sendVADEvent are no-ops, and there is no scripted playback of transcript/translation events anywhere. So picking "Demo (no backend)" in Settings connects, shows "Listening", and then nothing ever happens — no captions, no translation, forever.

Fix (minimal viable scripted playback):

ts
// add inside MockStreamingClient
private script = [
  { text: "Hi, can everyone hear me okay?", translated: "Hola, ¿me escuchan bien?" },
  { text: "Let's get started with today's agenda.", translated: "Empecemos con la agenda de hoy." },
]
private index = 0

connect(): void {
  if (!this.stopped) return
  this.stopped = false
  this.setConnectionState("connecting")
  const id = window.setTimeout(() => {
    this.timers.delete(id)
    if (this.stopped) return
    this.setConnectionState("connected")
    this.handlers.onEvent({
      type: "session_started",
      session_id: this.sessionId,
      configuration: { ...this.configuration, session_id: this.sessionId },
    })
    this.playNext()
  }, 300)
  this.timers.add(id)
}

private playNext(): void {
  if (this.stopped) return
  const item = this.script[this.index % this.script.length]
  const segId = `mock-${this.index}`
  this.index += 1
  const finalId = window.setTimeout(() => {
    this.timers.delete(finalId)
    if (this.stopped) return
    this.handlers.onEvent({
      type: "final_transcript", session_id: this.sessionId,
      segment_id: segId, text: item.text, is_final: true,
    })
    this.handlers.onEvent({
      type: "translation", session_id: this.sessionId, segment_id: segId,

3. (Resource leak) Silero VAD Web Worker is never terminated

Files: frontend/src/providers/vad/sileroVADProvider.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useAudioCapture.ts

Every Start press creates a brand-new SileroVADProvider, which lazily creates a brand-new Worker and loads the ~2MB ONNX model into it. On Stop, useAudioCapture.teardown() calls vadProviderRef.current?.stop() (which only posts a "reset" message) and then discards the reference — the underlying Worker and its WASM session are never terminated. Repeated Start/Stop cycles leak a Worker + inference session every time, and each restart pays the full ~1-2s model reload cost again.

Fix:

ts
// sileroVADProvider.ts — add a dispose method
dispose(): void {
  this.stopped = true
  this.worker?.terminate()
  this.worker = null
  this.initPromise = null
  this.eventHandlers.clear()
  this.stateHandlers.clear()
  this.probabilityHandlers.clear()
}
ts
// useAudioCapture.ts, in teardown():
vadProviderRef.current?.stop()
vadProviderRef.current?.dispose()   // <-- add this
vadProviderRef.current = null

Prompt you can give: "SileroVADProvider has no way to terminate its Worker. useAudioCapture.ts's teardown() discards the provider on every stop without releasing it, leaking a Worker + ONNX inference session per Start/Stop cycle. Add a dispose() method to SileroVADProvider that calls this.worker?.terminate() and clears listeners, and call it from teardown() right before nulling vadProviderRef.current."

4. (Correctness) Reconnect can permanently fail with session_in_use

Files: backend/app/websocket/translate_stream.py, frontend/src/lib/wsClient.ts

TranslatorClient has real reconnect/backoff logic, and on reconnect it replays the same session_id. But the backend keys a Session to a specific WebSocket object (SessionManager), and only releases it when the original connection's receive loop raises WebSocketDisconnect (its finally block calls session.stop()). If the network drop isn't detected as a clean close on the server side before the client reconnects (common on flaky Wi-Fi), the reconnecting client's session_configuration hits:

python
elif session.websocket is not websocket:
    await _send_error(websocket, "session_in_use", ...)
    return current

so reconnection with the same session_id fails until the stale connection eventually times out on its own.

Fix (backend): when a reconfiguration arrives for a session whose old websocket is already closed, replace it instead of rejecting:

python
elif session.websocket is not websocket:
    if session.websocket.client_state == WebSocketState.DISCONNECTED:
        session.websocket = websocket  # stale owner; take over
    else:
        await _send_error(websocket, "session_in_use", f"Session {config.session_id} belongs to another connection")
        return current

(from starlette.websockets import WebSocketState needs importing.)

Check session.websocket.client_state and, if it's WebSocketState.DISCONNECTED, take over the session on the new websocket instead of erroring."

5. (Critical, silent correctness bug) NLLB translations ignore the source language entirely

File: backend/app/services/translation/nllb_provider.py

python
async def translate(self, *, segment_id, text, source_language, target_language, is_final):
    ...
    nllb_code(source_language)   # validated, then thrown away
    nllb_code(target_language)
    translated = await asyncio.to_thread(
        self._translate_engine, text, source_language, target_language
    )
    ...

def _translate_engine(self, text, source_language, target_language):
    import torch
    tokenizer = self._tokenizer
    model = self._model
    target_token = nllb_code(target_language)
    inputs = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=...)
    # source_language is never referenced again below
    ...

source_language is accepted as a parameter but never used inside _translate_engine. NLLB's tokenizer needs tokenizer.src_lang set to the FLORES code (nllb_code(source_language)) before encoding — this is what tells the multilingual tokenizer which source-language special token to prepend. Since it's never set, every call silently uses whatever tokenizer.src_lang defaults to (typically eng_Latn), meaning any non-English source language produces wrong/garbled translations via the NLLB fallback path, with no error raised — it just quietly mistranslates. This is worse than a crash because it's invisible in the tests (they monkeypatch _translate_engine entirely, so the missing src_lang assignment is never exercised).

There's a secondary issue: the (model_name, device)-keyed tokenizer is shared process-wide across sessions (_MODEL_CACHE), and each translation runs on its own asyncio.to_thread worker thread. If two sessions translate concurrently with different source languages, mutating tokenizer.src_lang on the shared object is a data race — one session's request can pick up another's src_lang.

Fix:

python
def _translate_engine(self, text: str, source_language: str, target_language: str) -> str:
    import torch

    tokenizer = self._tokenizer
    model = self._model
    tokenizer.src_lang = nllb_code(source_language)   # <-- set before encoding
    target_token = nllb_code(target_language)
    inputs = tokenizer(
        text,
        return_tensors="pt",
        truncation=True,
        max_length=self._settings.nllb_max_length,
    )
    with torch.inference_mode():
        outputs = model.generate(
            **inputs,
            forced_bos_token_id=tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(target_token),
            max_length=self._settings.nllb_max_length,
            num_beams=self._settings.nllb_num_beams,
        )
    return tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True)

And guard against the cross-session race by serializing calls to the shared tokenizer, e.g. add a module-level threading.Lock() around the tokenizer.src_lang = ... → tokenizer(text, ...) span in _translate_engine (or give each provider instance/session its own tokenizer copy instead of sharing the tokenizer object, while still sharing the heavier model weights).

Prompt you can give: "In backend/app/services/translation/nllb_provider.py, _translate_engine never sets tokenizer.src_lang before encoding, so source_language is effectively ignored and NLLB translations use the tokenizer's default source language for every call regardless of the actual spoken language. Add tokenizer.src_lang = nllb_code(source_language) right before the tokenizer(text, ...) call in _translate_engine, and add a threading.Lock around that mutate-then-encode span since the tokenizer is shared process-wide across concurrent sessions via _MODEL_CACHE."

6. (Config footgun) Default settings guarantee translation always fails until the user changes something

Files: frontend/src/config/preferences.ts, .env.example, backend/app/services/translation/languages.py

Out of the box:

preferences.ts defaults sourceLanguage: "auto".
.env.example ships TRANSLATION_PROVIDER=hybrid with CLOUD_TRANSLATION_API_KEY= blank.
HybridTranslationProvider tries cloud first → CloudTranslationProvider raises cloud_config immediately (no key) → falls back to NLLB → NLLBTranslationProvider.translate() calls nllb_code("auto"), which is hard-coded to always raise TranslationError("unsupported_language", ...) (NLLB has no auto-detect).

So with a completely unconfigured backend and the app's own default UI language selection, translation fails on every single utterance (surfaced to the user as a non-fatal translation_failed error banner each time), even though ASR/captions work fine. It's not a code bug exactly, but it's a real functional trap: nothing in the UI explains why translation never succeeds, and the failure mode is silent/repeating rather than a clear one-time "configure a provider" message.

Fix options (pick one):

Cheapest: change the default sourceLanguage in preferences.ts from "auto" to a concrete language (e.g. "en"), so the NLLB-only fallback path at least has a chance of working without cloud credentials.
Better: have the backend detect "no provider fully configured" at startup (no cloud key and no offline extra installed) and surface a clearer one-time error event / log warning rather than a translation_failed per utterance, so a fresh clone is diagnosable.

Prompt you can give: "The app's default sourceLanguage is 'auto' (frontend/src/config/preferences.ts), but NLLBTranslationProvider rejects 'auto' by design (no offline language detection) and the default .env.example ships with no cloud translation API key. This means a fresh, unconfigured install has 100% translation failure by default with no clear signal why. Either change the default sourceLanguage to a concrete language code, or add a startup check in backend/app/main.py/create_translation_provider() that logs a clear one-time warning when neither cloud credentials nor a usable offline provider are configured."

<content>
1: # Real-Time Translator
2: 
3: A real-time, multilingual speech translator for online meetings (Zoom, Google Meet, etc.).
4: Streams live speech to text, translates it, and displays translated captions with
5: minimal latency — with silence detection used to produce clean sentence boundaries
6: and punctuation. It ships as a compact, always-on-top **desktop companion window**
7: (Electron) that sits beside your meeting and shows live translations while you talk.
8: 
9: > **Status:** the backend now streams live transcripts through **Deepgram
10: > streaming ASR** (Phase 1) and translates finalized utterances through a
11: > **hybrid cloud → NLLB-200 fallback** pipeline (Phase 2): interim/final
12: > results, punctuation + smart formatting, multilingual / language-detection,
13: > client-silence-driven utterance finalization, automatic reconnects, and
14: > measured ASR **and** translation **and** LLM-refinement latency. The backend
15: > boots, serves `/health`, and passes 95 tests (transport + Deepgram provider
16: > suite against a fake server + language-registry/cloud/NLLB/hybrid provider
17: > suites + LLM refinement provider/transport suites); the frontend typechecks,
18: > lints, builds, and renders real-time partial/final transcripts that freeze on
19: > finalization, plus live translations and post-hoc refined transcripts.
20: 
21: ## What this is
22: 
23: - **ASR:** Deepgram Streaming API (default), behind an `ASRProvider` interface.
24: - **Translation:** hybrid — a low-latency cloud provider by default, with NLLB-200
25:   as an offline/fallback provider, behind a `TranslationProvider` interface.
26: - **VAD (silence detection):** client-side Silero VAD running in an AudioWorklet,
27:   so silence detection never adds server round-trip latency.
28: - **LLM refinement:** an async, post-hoc pass that improves punctuation,
29:   capitalization, obvious ASR errors, and contextual terminology — it runs
30:   **after** an utterance is finalized and is never on the latency-critical path.
31: 
32: ## Project structure
33: 
34: ```
35: real-time-translator/
36: ├── electron/         Electron desktop companion window
37: │   ├── main.js         main process: compact always-on-top window, window-state
38: │   │                   persistence, backend auto-start, window IPC
39: │   ├── preload.js      contextBridge: exposes only window.desktop controls
40: │   └── package.json    dev scripts (backend + vite + electron together)
41: ├── frontend/          React + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind UI
42: │   └── src/
43: │       ├── components/  CompactHeader, LanguageBar, TranscriptView,
44: │       │                TranslationView, ListeningControls, SettingsModal, ...
45: │       ├── hooks/       useTranslatorSession, useAudioCapture
46: │       ├── providers/   vad/ (VADProvider interface + SileroVADProvider stub)
47: │       ├── lib/         wsClient.ts (TranslatorClient WebSocket wrapper)
48: │       ├── types/       shared types mirroring backend schemas
49: │       └── styles/      Tailwind entrypoint
50: ├── backend/           FastAPI + asyncio + WebSocket pipeline
51: │   ├── app/             main.py, config.py, websocket/, services/ (asr,
52: │   │                    translation, vad, llm), models/, utils/
53: │   └── tests/           pytest suite (health, config, websocket, VAD,
54: │                        Deepgram ASR, languages, translation providers)
55: ├── docs/              Supplementary docs
56: ├── tests/             Cross-cutting / integration tests (root level)
57: ├── .env.example       All environment variables, documented
58: ├── .gitignore
59: ├── README.md          You are here
60: ├── ARCHITECTURE.md    System design, data flow, provider abstractions
61: └── DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md  Phased build-out plan and current status
62: ```
63: 
64: See `ARCHITECTURE.md` for the full system design and `backend/app/services/*`
65: for the provider interfaces (`ASRProvider`, `TranslationProvider`, `LLMProvider`)
66: that keep business logic decoupled from any single vendor.
67: 
68: ## Prerequisites
69: 
70: - Python 3.11+ (backend core). Tested on 3.14.
71: - Node.js 20+ and npm (frontend).
72: - [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for Python dependency management (recommended),
73:   or plain `pip` + `venv`.
74: - API keys for whichever providers you enable (Deepgram, a cloud translation
75:   provider, an LLM provider) — see `.env.example`. None are required to run the
76:   scaffold: `/health` and the frontend shell need no external providers.
77: 
78: > Python version note: the backend pins `requires-python = ">=3.11"`. The core
79: > dependencies run fine on 3.14. Only the *offline* extra (`torch`,
80: > `transformers`, for NLLB-200) is constrained to 3.11/3.12 because those
81: > packages do not yet ship stable wheels for 3.14 — install it with
82: > `uv sync --extra offline` only if you need the offline fallback.
83: 
84: ## Getting started
85: 
86: ### Backend
87: 
88: ```bash
89: cd backend
90: uv sync                         # creates/updates .venv and installs deps
91: cp ../.env.example .env         # then fill in DEEPGRAM_API_KEY etc. (optional)
92: uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
93: ```
94: 
95: Verify it's up:
96: 
97: ```bash
98: curl http://localhost:8000/health
99: # {"status":"ok","env":"development","asr_provider":"deepgram","translation_provider":"hybrid"}
100: ```
101: 
102: ### Frontend
103: 
104: ```bash
105: cd frontend
106: npm install
107: npm run dev
108: ```
109: 
110: Open the URL Vite prints (default `http://localhost:5173`). The Vite dev server
111: proxies `/api` and `/ws` to `http://localhost:8000` (see `frontend/vite.config.ts`),
112: so the frontend and backend can be developed independently.
113: 
114: ### Running checks
115: 
116: ```bash
117: # Backend: lint + tests
118: cd backend && uv run ruff check .
119: cd backend && uv run pytest
120: 
121: # Frontend: lint + typecheck + build
122: cd frontend && npm run lint
123: cd frontend && npm run typecheck
124: cd frontend && npm run build
125: ```
126: 
127: ## Desktop companion (Electron)
128: 
129: The translator runs as a small floating window that stays on top of your meeting
130: (Zoom, Meet, Teams). It is **not** a full-screen site.
131: 
132: ### Start everything at once
133: 
134: ```bash
135: npm run install:all   # first time: install frontend + electron deps
136: npm run dev           # starts FastAPI backend + Vite dev server + Electron
137: ```
138: 
139: `npm run dev` is defined in the **electron** package and uses `concurrently` to
140: run all three together: the backend on `:8000`, Vite on `:5173`, and Electron
141: (which waits on both ports, then loads `http://localhost:5173`).
142: 
143: Individual pieces (useful while iterating):
144: 
145: ```bash
146: npm run dev:backend    # uvicorn with --reload
147: npm run dev:frontend   # Vite only (browser tab, no window chrome)
148: npm run dev:electron   # Electron only (uses already-running backend + Vite)
149: ```
150: 
151: To run Electron against the **built** renderer instead of the dev server:
152: 
153: ```bash
154: npm run start   # builds frontend/dist, then launches Electron (loads file://)
155: ```
156: 
157: ### Window behavior
158: 
159: - Compact companion window (~420×600), `alwaysOnTop` ("floating" level), movable
160:   by dragging the header, resizable, minimizable.
161: - Size and position are remembered between launches (`window-state.json`).
162: - Pin/unpin button toggles always-on-top.
163: - Two display modes: **Expanded** (source transcript + translation + language
164:   selectors) and **Compact** (translation only). Switch via the header.
165: - Debug-only details (latency, WS events, audio diagnostics) are hidden unless
166:   the app was built for development and are exposed only through Settings.
167: 
168: ### Security model
169: 
170: The renderer runs with `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`,
171: `sandbox: true`, and `webSecurity: true`. The preload script exposes **only**
172: `window.desktop` (minimize/close/pin/always-on-top) via `contextBridge` — no
173: Node APIs reach the React code. See `electron/main.js` + `electron/preload.js`
174: and the Electron section in `ARCHITECTURE.md`.
175: 
176: The renderer still talks to FastAPI exactly as before over the existing
177: WebSocket protocol — the desktop shell adds no new AI pipeline code and changes
178: nothing in ASR/translation/WebSocket handling.
179: 
180: ## Design principles
181: 
182: 1. **Provider abstractions everywhere.** `ASRProvider`, `TranslationProvider`,
183:    `LLMProvider`, and a client-side `VADProvider` mean no business logic is
184:    tightly coupled to Deepgram, a specific translation API, or a specific LLM.
185: 2. **Latency-critical path stays lean.** ASR → translation → display is the hot
186:    path. LLM refinement is strictly async and only ever *improves* text already
187:    shown to the user — it never blocks it.
188: 3. **Silence is signal.** Client-side VAD silence events double as endpointing
189:    hints, giving cleaner sentence boundaries and punctuation than relying on
190:    ASR endpointing alone.
191: 4. **UI needs no manual.** Two panels (original / translation), one big
192:    start/stop control, obvious connection and latency indicators.
193: 
194: ## Roadmap
195: 
196: See `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md` for the phased plan, from this scaffold through
197: production hardening and system/meeting-audio ingestion.

(End of file - total 197 lines)
</content>
```

Wrap the existing React application using Electron.

Create a compact translator window.

* supports minimize

22: - **ASR:** Deepgram Streaming API (default), behind an `ASRProvider` interface.
23: - **Translation:** hybrid — a low-latency cloud provider by default, with NLLB-200
24:   as an offline/fallback provider, behind a `TranslationProvider` interface.
25: - **VAD (silence detection):** client-side Silero VAD running in an AudioWorklet,
26:   so silence detection never adds server round-trip latency.
27: - **LLM refinement:** an async, post-hoc pass that improves punctuation,
28:   capitalization, obvious ASR errors, and contextual terminology — it runs
29:   **after** an utterance is finalized and is never on the latency-critical path.
30: 
31: ## Project structure
32: 
33: ```
34: real-time-translator/
35: ├── frontend/          React + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind UI
36: │   └── src/
37: │       ├── components/  LanguageSelector, AudioControls, ConnectionStatus,
38: │       │                LatencyIndicator, ErrorBanner, TranscriptPanel,
39: │       │                TranslationPanel
40: │       ├── hooks/       useTranslatorSession, useAudioCapture
41: │       ├── providers/   vad/ (VADProvider interface + SileroVADProvider stub)
42: │       ├── lib/         wsClient.ts (TranslatorClient WebSocket wrapper)
43: │       ├── types/       shared types mirroring backend schemas
44: │       └── styles/      Tailwind entrypoint
45: ├── backend/           FastAPI + asyncio + WebSocket pipeline
46: │   ├── app/             main.py, config.py, websocket/, services/ (asr,
47: │   │                    translation, vad, llm), models/, utils/
48: │   └── tests/           pytest suite (health, config, websocket, VAD,
49: │                        Deepgram ASR, languages, translation providers)
50: ├── docs/              Supplementary docs
51: ├── tests/             Cross-cutting / integration tests (root level)
52: ├── .env.example       All environment variables, documented
53: ├── .gitignore
54: ├── README.md          You are here
55: ├── ARCHITECTURE.md    System design, data flow, provider abstractions
56: └── DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md  Phased build-out plan and current status
57: ```
58: 
59: See `ARCHITECTURE.md` for the full system design and `backend/app/services/*`
60: for the provider interfaces (`ASRProvider`, `TranslationProvider`, `LLMProvider`)
61: that keep business logic decoupled from any single vendor.
62: 
63: ## Prerequisites
64: 
65: - Python 3.11+ (backend core). Tested on 3.14.
66: - Node.js 20+ and npm (frontend).
67: - [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for Python dependency management (recommended),
68:   or plain `pip` + `venv`.
69: - API keys for whichever providers you enable (Deepgram, a cloud translation
70:   provider, an LLM provider) — see `.env.example`. None are required to run the
71:   scaffold: `/health` and the frontend shell need no external providers.
72: 
73: > Python version note: the backend pins `requires-python = ">=3.11"`. The core
74: > dependencies run fine on 3.14. Only the *offline* extra (`torch`,
75: > `transformers`, for NLLB-200) is constrained to 3.11/3.12 because those
76: > packages do not yet ship stable wheels for 3.14 — install it with
77: > `uv sync --extra offline` only if you need the offline fallback.
78: 
79: ## Getting started
80: 
81: ### Backend
82: 
83: ```bash
84: cd backend
85: uv sync                         # creates/updates .venv and installs deps
86: cp ../.env.example .env         # then fill in DEEPGRAM_API_KEY etc. (optional)
87: uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
88: ```
89: 
90: Verify it's up:
91: 
92: ```bash
93: curl http://localhost:8000/health
94: # {"status":"ok","env":"development","asr_provider":"deepgram","translation_provider":"hybrid"}
95: ```
96: 
97: ### Frontend
98: 
99: ```bash
100: cd frontend
101: npm install
102: npm run dev
103: ```
104: 
105: Open the URL Vite prints (default `http://localhost:5173`). The Vite dev server
106: proxies `/api` and `/ws` to `http://localhost:8000` (see `frontend/vite.config.ts`),
107: so the frontend and backend can be developed independently.

109: ### Running checks
110: 
111: ```bash

113: cd backend && uv run ruff check .
114: cd backend && uv run pytest
115: 
116: # Frontend: lint + typecheck + build
117: cd frontend && npm run lint
118: cd frontend && npm run typecheck
119: cd frontend && npm run build
120: ```
121: 
122: ## Design principles
123: 
124: 1. **Provider abstractions everywhere.** `ASRProvider`, `TranslationProvider`,
125:    `LLMProvider`, and a client-side `VADProvider` mean no business logic is
126:    tightly coupled to Deepgram, a specific translation API, or a specific LLM.
127: 2. **Latency-critical path stays lean.** ASR → translation → display is the hot
128:    path. LLM refinement is strictly async and only ever *improves* text already
129:    shown to the user — it never blocks it.
130: 3. **Silence is signal.** Client-side VAD silence events double as endpointing
131:    hints, giving cleaner sentence boundaries and punctuation than relying on
132:    ASR endpointing alone.
133: 4. **UI needs no manual.** Two panels (original / translation), one big
134:    start/stop control, obvious connection and latency indicators.
135: 
136: ## Roadmap
137: 
138: See `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md` for the phased plan, from this scaffold through
139: production hardening and system/meeting-audio ingestion.

1: # Architecture
2: 
3: ## 1. Goals and constraints
4: 
5: - **Low latency end-to-end.** Speech must appear as translated captions within a
6:   few hundred milliseconds, not seconds.
7: - **Provider independence.** Deepgram, the cloud translation API, NLLB-200, and
8:   the LLM refinement provider must all be swappable without touching pipeline
9:   or UI code. This is enforced with abstract provider interfaces.
10: - **Correctness improves without blocking speed.** Punctuation/terminology
11:   refinement is valuable but must never sit on the hot path.
12: - **Silence is a first-class signal**, not just "no audio" — it's used both to
13:   save bandwidth/compute and to produce clean sentence boundaries.
14: - **Extensible to meeting audio.** The pipeline should not assume "microphone"
15:   as the only audio source; system/meeting audio capture is a planned input,
16:   not an architectural afterthought.
17: 
18: ## 2. High-level data flow
19: 
20: ```
21: ┌─────────────┐   PCM frames    ┌──────────────────┐
22: │  Microphone /│ ───────────────▶│  Silero VAD       │  (AudioWorklet, client-side)
23: │  meeting audio│                │  speech/silence   │
24: └─────────────┘                 └─────────┬─────────┘
25:                                            │ speech_start / speech_end events
26:                                            ▼
27:                               ┌────────────────────────┐
28:                               │  Audio capture pipeline  │  (client-side)
29:                               │  getUserMedia → Worklet  │
30:                               └────────────┬─────────────┘
31:                                            │ 16kHz PCM frames + silence events
32:                                            ▼  (WebSocket, binary + JSON control)
33:                               ┌────────────────────────┐
34:                                │   FastAPI WS endpoint    │  backend/app/websocket
35:                                │   /ws/translate           │
36:                               └────────────┬─────────────┘
37:                                            │
38:                           ┌────────────────┼────────────────┐
39:                           ▼                                   ▼
40:               ┌─────────────────────┐             notify_silence() hints
41:               │   ASRProvider         │◀───────────────────────────────┐
42:               │   (Deepgram default)  │                                 │
43:               └───────────┬───────────┘                                 │
44:                           │ partial + final TranscriptSegment            │
45:                           ▼                                              │
46:               ┌─────────────────────┐                                   │
47:               │  TranslationProvider  │  hybrid: cloud (default) ────────┘
48:               │  cloud / NLLB          │  or NLLB-200 (fallback/offline)
49:               └───────────┬───────────┘
50:                           │ partial + final TranslationSegment
51:                           ▼
52:               ┌─────────────────────┐        (fire-and-forget, async)
53:               │  Client (React UI)    │◀────────────┐
54:               │  transcript + captions │             │
55:               └───────────┬───────────┘             │
56:                           │ final segment id          │
57:                           ▼                            │
58:               ┌─────────────────────┐                 │
59:               │   LLMProvider          │────────────────┘
60:               │   async refinement pass │  REFINEMENT event, replaces
61:               └─────────────────────┘  displayed text in place, non-blocking
62: ```
63: 
64: Key point: **the LLM box is not in the request/response chain that produces the
65: first visible caption.** It's triggered after a segment is finalized, runs in
66: a background asyncio task, and pushes a correction later via a separate
67: `refinement` WebSocket event. The UI already has *something* on screen; the
68: refinement just makes it better.
69: 
70: ## 3. Provider abstractions
71: 
72: All providers are ABCs so the pipeline/orchestrator and the UI depend only on
73: interfaces, never concrete vendors.
74: 
75: ### `ASRProvider` (`backend/app/services/asr/base.py`)
76: 
77: ```
78: connect(sample_rate, encoding, language) -> None
79: send_audio(chunk: bytes) -> None
80: notify_silence(duration_ms: int) -> None
81: stream() -> AsyncIterator[TranscriptSegment]
82: close() -> None
83: ```
84: 
85: `DeepgramASRProvider` is the default implementation. `notify_silence` maps to
86: Deepgram's endpointing/finalize controls, letting client-detected silence force
87: a clean utterance boundary rather than waiting on server-side heuristics alone.
88: 
89: It talks to Deepgram's `/v1/listen` WebSocket directly (via `websockets`, not
90: the SDK) so the failure/backoff behavior is fully under our control and is
91: testable against a fake server:
92: 
93: - `connect()` never blocks on the network. It spawns a **reader** task (owns
94:   the connection, reconnects with exponential backoff, base
95:   `deepgram_reconnect_base_delay_ms`, capped at `deepgram_reconnect_max_attempts`)
96:   and a **sender** task that drains a bounded audio queue, so streaming audio
97:   in never back-pressures the browser → backend WebSocket (oldest frames are
98:   dropped on overflow during a reconnect).
99: - `partial_transcript` results are forwarded the moment they arrive; finals are
100:   emitted on utterance end (Deepgram endpointing / `Finalize` / `UtteranceEnd`).
101:   Empty finals and duplicate finals are dropped; segment ids are stable
102:   (`<uid>-<n>`) so the UI can update a partial in place and freeze it on final.
103: - Failure codes (`ASRProviderError.code`): `deepgram_config` (missing API key),
104:   `deepgram_auth` (HTTP 401/403 or Error message), `deepgram_connection`
105:   (unreachable after retries), `deepgram_error` (Deepgram `Error` message),
106:   `deepgram_closed`. A fatal error surfaces once on `stream()` and tears down
107:   the session.
108: - `asr_latency_ms` on each `TranscriptSegment` estimates audio-received →
109:   ASR-result latency by interpolating the streaming timeline; the transport
110:   surfaces it as the `asr_ms` field of a `latency` WS event.
111: 
112: ### `TranslationProvider` (`backend/app/services/translation/base.py`)
113: 
114: ```
115: translate(segment_id, text, source_language, target_language, is_final) -> TranslationSegment
116: warm_up() -> None            # optional: load models / open connections
117: health_check() -> bool       # optional: used by the hybrid router
118: close() -> None              # optional: release HTTP clients / loaded models
119: ```
120: 
121: Three implementations, selected by the `translation_provider` setting:
122: 
123: - `CloudTranslationProvider` — primary, low-latency path. Talks to Google
124:   Cloud Translation v2 REST directly with httpx (no SDK); endpoint and
125:   timeout configurable. Failure codes: `cloud_config`, `cloud_connection`,
126:   `cloud_translation_error`.
127: - `NLLBTranslationProvider` — offline fallback using the NLLB-200
128:   distilled-600M model. Loads lazily in a thread on first use; raises
129:   `translation_failed`/`nllb_model_unavailable` if the runtime can't load it.
130: - `HybridTranslationProvider` — default. Tries cloud first; on any
131:   `TranslationError` it falls back to NLLB for that utterance. Both failing
132:   raises `TranslationError("translation_failed")`. A transient cloud failure
133:   therefore degrades one utterance instead of failing the meeting.
134: 
135: Language codes are resolved centrally in `languages.py` (each `Language`:
136: `iso_code`, `display_name`, `cloud_code`, `nllb_code` FLORES-200 token); the
137: pipeline never branches on language pairs. `create_translation_provider()` in
138: `translation/__init__.py` is the only entry point the transport uses. See
139: `docs/translation.md` for the full design.
140: 
141: ### `LLMProvider` (`backend/app/services/llm/base.py`)
142: 
143: ```
144: refine(segment_id, text, language, context) -> RefinementResult
145: ```
146: 
147: `LLMRefinementProvider` is the default implementation. `context` is a short
148: window of recent finalized segments so terminology stays consistent across an
149: utterance or meeting (e.g. a company/product name transcribed inconsistently).
150: 
151: ### `VADProvider` (frontend: `frontend/src/providers/vad/types.ts`)
152: 
153: VAD runs **client-side** for latency reasons (a round-trip to the server just
154: to learn "the user stopped talking" would defeat the purpose). The interface:
155: 
156: ```
157: init() -> Promise<void>                       # load model in background; never blocks
158: start() -> Promise<void>                      # begin processing worklet frames
159: stop() -> Promise<void>                       # stop + reset the state machine
160: processFrame(samples: Float32Array) -> void   # feed one 512-sample window @ 16 kHz
161: onEvent(cb: (e: VADEvent) => void) -> () => void
162: onStateChange(cb: (s: VADStatus) => void) -> () => void
163: onProbability(cb: (p: number) => void) -> () => void   # throttled, diagnostics
164: configure(partial: Partial<VADConfig>) -> void          # live threshold changes
165: state -> VADStatus                            # idle | loading | speaking | silence | error
166: ```
167: 
168: The pipeline (see `docs/vad.md` for the full write-up):
169: 
170: - The **AudioWorklet** (`pcmCaptureWorklet.js`) does capture + resampling +
171:   PCM16 streaming exactly as before. It additionally emits the same 16 kHz
172:   stream as 512-sample Float32 windows for VAD — so streaming is **never
173:   blocked** by VAD inference.
174: - **`SileroVADProvider`** (`sileroVADProvider.ts`) is a thin main-thread wrapper
175:   over a dedicated **Web Worker** (`sileroVADWorker.ts`) that runs the Silero
176:   VAD v5 ONNX model with onnxruntime-web (WASM). Model loading is
177:   fire-and-forget; frames arriving before the model is ready are buffered
178:   (bounded) in the worker and replayed.
179: - The worker emits five lifecycle events: `speech_started`, `speaking`
180:   (heartbeat while active), `silence_started` (transient, after the hangover),
181:   `silence_detected` (utterance boundary after the configurable silence
182:   threshold), and `speech_resumed`. A 100 ms pause therefore produces no
183:   boundary; a 600 ms pause produces `silence_detected` (with `duration_ms`).
184: - Events are forwarded to the UI (● Speaking / ○ Silence detected) and, in
185:   live mode, to the backend as `vad_event` messages that the ASR provider can
186:   use as endpointing hints later.
187: 
188: The backend also defines a `SilenceDetector` helper
189: (`backend/app/services/vad/base.py`) that turns raw silence-duration reports
190: into a "should this finalize the utterance?" decision, using two tunables:
191: - `SILENCE_FINALIZE_MS` — how much silence implies "sentence is over".
192: - `SILENCE_MIN_SPEECH_MS` — minimum preceding speech to avoid false triggers
193:   from breath sounds / noise.
194: 
195: ## 4. Why VAD is client-side but the interface lives on both sides
196: 
197: Silero VAD executes in the browser for latency. But the *concept* of "was this
198: gap in audio significant enough to be a sentence boundary" is also useful
199: server-side (e.g. if audio ever arrives from a source without a client
200: worklet — a recorded meeting file, or server-side capture of meeting audio).
201: That's why there's a `VADProvider` interface on the frontend for the live
202: capture path, and a separate `SilenceDetector`/`VADProvider` on the backend for
203: interpreting silence signals and, later, for any server-side VAD fallback —
204: without changing how the ASR/translation pipeline consumes "silence happened
205: here" events.
206: 
207: ## 5. WebSocket protocol
208: 
209: Single endpoint: `ws://<backend>/ws/translate`. See
210: `backend/app/models/schemas.py` for exact payloads. Every message is a JSON
211: envelope of the form `{"type": "<message>", ...fields}`; audio frames travel as
212: raw binary WebSocket messages rather than base64-encoded JSON.
213: 
214: **Client → Server**
215: | Message | Shape |
216: |---|---|
217: | Start session | `{"type": "start_session", "session_id"?: str}` |
218: | Session configuration | `{"type": "session_configuration", session_id, source_language, target_language, audio_source, sample_rate?, encoding?}` |
219: | Audio | binary WebSocket frame (raw PCM16 or Opus) |
220: | Audio chunk (control) | `{"type": "audio_chunk", "session_id": str}` |
221: | VAD event | `{"type": "vad_event", session_id, event, timestamp_ms, duration_ms?, probability?}` — `event` ∈ `speech_started \| speaking \| silence_started \| silence_detected \| speech_resumed` |
222: | Stop session | `{"type": "stop_session", "session_id": str}` |
223: 
224: **Server → Client**
225: | Message | Shape |
226: |---|---|
227: | Session started | `{"type": "session_started", session_id, configuration}` |
228: | Speech lifecycle | `{"type": "speech_started" \| "silence_detected" \| "speech_resumed", session_id, timestamp_ms, duration_ms?}` |
229: | Partial/final transcript | `{"type": "partial_transcript" \| "final_transcript", session_id, ...TranscriptEvent}` |
230: | Translation | `{"type": "translation", session_id, ...TranslationEvent}` |
231: | Async refinement | `{"type": "refined_transcript", session_id, segment_id, refined_text, changed}` |
232: | Latency report | `{"type": "latency", session_id, segment_id, asr_ms, translation_ms, end_to_end_ms}` |
233: | Error | `{"type": "error", code, message, session_id?}` |
234: | Session stopped | `{"type": "session_stopped", session_id, reason}` |
235: 
236: ## 6. Frontend structure
237: 
238: ```
239: frontend/src/
240: ├── components/         one folder per reusable UI piece (own file + index.ts)
241: │   ├── LanguageSelector/
242: │   ├── AudioControls/
243: │   ├── ConnectionStatus/
244: │   ├── LatencyIndicator/
245: │   ├── ErrorBanner/
246: │   ├── TranscriptPanel/
247: │   └── TranslationPanel/
248: ├── hooks/
249: │   ├── useTranslatorSession.ts   orchestrates connection + pipeline state
250: │   └── useAudioCapture.ts        getUserMedia + AudioWorklet plumbing
251: ├── providers/
252: │   └── vad/                      VADProvider interface + SileroVADProvider
253: ├── lib/
254: │   └── wsClient.ts                thin WebSocket transport (TranslatorClient)
255: ├── types/                         shared types mirroring backend schemas
256: ├── styles/                        Tailwind entrypoint
257: ├── App.tsx                        UI shell: selectors, controls, two panels
258: └── main.tsx
259: ```
260: 
261: `useTranslatorSession` is the single seam between UI and networking/audio —
262: components never touch `WebSocket` or `MediaStream` directly, which keeps the
263: UI layer trivial to test and restyle.
264: 
265: ## 7. Backend structure
266: 
267: ```
268: backend/app/
269: ├── main.py              FastAPI app: CORS, router mounting, /health
270: ├── config.py             pydantic-settings Settings, env-driven
271: ├── websocket/
272: │   └── translate_stream.py  /ws/translate transport layer (thin) + SessionManager
273: ├── services/
274: │   ├── asr/               ASRProvider + DeepgramASRProvider
275: │   ├── translation/        TranslationProvider + Cloud/NLLB implementations
276: │   ├── vad/                 VADProvider + SilenceDetector
277: │   └── llm/                  LLMProvider + LLMRefinementProvider
278: ├── models/
279: │   └── schemas.py          shared Pydantic models (WS + internal)
280: └── utils/
281:     └── logging.py           structlog setup
282: ```
283: 
284: Notice `websocket/translate_stream.py` stays thin on purpose — it's transport, not
285: orchestration. As Phase 2 (see `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md`) lands, a
286: `PipelineOrchestrator` (or similar) will sit between the transport layer and
287: the providers, owning per-session state, provider selection, and the async
288: refinement dispatch — keeping the WebSocket handler itself simple regardless
289: of how complex the pipeline gets.
290: 
291: ## 8. Path to meeting/system audio
292: 
293: Today's design already generalizes past "microphone": the WebSocket protocol
294: and `ASRProvider` interface don't care where PCM frames come from. Consuming
295: Zoom/Meet system audio is a matter of adding a capture source (e.g. a
296: platform-level loopback capture, a meeting-bot integration, or a browser tab
297: audio capture) that feeds the same `useAudioCapture` → WebSocket → `ASRProvider`
298: path. No changes to ASR, translation, VAD-interpretation, or refinement layers
299: are expected.
300: 
301: ## 9. Latency budget (target, for tuning once implemented)
302: 
303: | Stage | Target |
304: |---|---|
305: | Client capture → WS send | < 20 ms |
306: | ASR partial result | < 300 ms |
307: | Translation (cloud) | < 150 ms |
308: | Translation (NLLB fallback) | 1–3 s, only on cloud failure |
309: | Total: speech → on-screen translation | < 500 ms |
310: | LLM refinement (async, non-blocking) | 1–3 s, off critical path |
311: 
312: These are targets to validate against. ASR latency is now actually measured
313: (`asr_ms` per segment) and translation latency is measured too (`translation_ms`
314: per segment, both surfaced via the `latency` WS event); end-to-end timing will
315: be validated against these targets once live providers are wired in.

26:   private reconnectTimer: number | null = null
27:   private startSessionId: string | null = null
28:   private configuration: SessionConfiguration | null = null
29: 
30:   constructor(private readonly handlers: StreamingClientHandlers) {}
31: 
32:   get isOpen(): boolean {
33:     return this.socket?.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN
34:   }
35: 
36:   connect(): void {
37:     if (this.socket) return
38:     this.explicitlyClosed = false
39:     this.setState("connecting")
40:     this.openSocket()
41:   }
42: 
43:   sendStartSession(sessionId: string): void {
44:     this.startSessionId = sessionId
45:     this.queue({ type: "start_session", session_id: sessionId })
46:   }
47: 
48:   sendConfiguration(config: SessionConfiguration): void {
49:     this.configuration = config
50:     this.queue({ type: "session_configuration", ...config })
51:   }
52: 
53:   sendAudio(bytes: Uint8Array): void {
54:     if (this.socket?.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) {
55:       this.socket.send(bytes)
56:     }
57:   }
58: 
59:   sendVADEvent(event: VADEvent): void {
60:     if (this.socket?.readyState !== WebSocket.OPEN || !this.startSessionId) return
61:     const message: ClientMessage = {
62:       type: "vad_event",
63:       session_id: this.startSessionId,
64:       event: event.type,
65:       timestamp_ms: event.timestamp,
66:     }
67:     if (event.durationMs !== undefined) message.duration_ms = event.durationMs
68:     if (event.probability !== undefined) message.probability = event.probability
69:     this.sendJson(message)
70:   }
71: 
72:   sendStopSession(sessionId: string): void {
73:     this.queue({ type: "stop_session", session_id: sessionId })
74:   }
75: 
76:   close(): void {
77:     this.explicitlyClosed = true
78:     this.stopReconnect()
79:     this.pending = []
80:     if (this.socket) {
81:       this.socket.onclose = null
82:       this.socket.close()
83:       this.socket = null
84:     }
85:     this.setState("idle")
86:   }
87: 
88:   private openSocket(): void {
89:     const socket = new WebSocket(wsUrl())
90:     this.socket = socket
91:     socket.binaryType = "arraybuffer"
92: 
93:     socket.onopen = () => {
94:       this.reconnectAttempts = 0
95:       if (this.startSessionId) {
96:         this.pending.unshift({ type: "start_session", session_id: this.startSessionId })
97:       }
98:       if (this.configuration) {
99:         this.pending.push({ type: "session_configuration", ...this.configuration })
100:       }
101:       this.flushQueue()
102:       this.setState("connected")
103:     }
104: 
105:     socket.onmessage = (event: MessageEvent) => {
106:       if (typeof event.data !== "string") return
107:       try {
108:         const data = JSON.parse(event.data) as ServerEvent
109:         this.handlers.onEvent(data)
110:       } catch {
111:         this.handlers.onError("Received a malformed message from the server")
112:       }
113:     }
114: 
115:     socket.onerror = () => {
116:       this.handlers.onError("WebSocket connection error")
117:     }
118: 
119:     socket.onclose = () => {
120:       if (this.socket !== socket) return
121:       this.socket = null
122:       if (this.explicitlyClosed) {
123:         this.setState("disconnected")
124:         return
125:       }
126:       this.scheduleReconnect()
127:     }
128:   }
129: 
130:   private queue(message: ClientMessage): void {
131:     if (this.socket?.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) {
132:       this.sendJson(message)
133:       return
134:     }
135:     this.pending.push(message)
136:   }
137: 
138:   private flushQueue(): void {
139:     const messages = this.pending
140:     this.pending = []
141:     for (const message of messages) {
142:       this.sendJson(message)
143:     }
144:   }
145: 
146:   private scheduleReconnect(): void {
147:     if (this.explicitlyClosed) return
148:     if (this.reconnectAttempts >= MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS) {
149:       this.setState("disconnected")
150:       this.handlers.onError("Connection lost. Reconnect attempts exhausted.")
151:       return
152:     }
153:     this.setState("reconnecting")
154:     const delay = RECONNECT_BASE_DELAY_MS * 2 ** this.reconnectAttempts
155:     this.reconnectAttempts += 1
156:     this.reconnectTimer = window.setTimeout(() => {
157:       this.reconnectTimer = null
158:       if (this.explicitlyClosed) return
159:       this.setState("reconnecting")
160:       this.openSocket()
161:     }, delay)
162:   }
163: 
164:   private stopReconnect(): void {
165:     if (this.reconnectTimer !== null) {
166:       window.clearTimeout(this.reconnectTimer)
167:       this.reconnectTimer = null
168:     }
169:   }
170: 
171:   private sendJson(payload: ClientMessage): void {
172:     if (this.socket?.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) {
173:       this.socket.send(JSON.stringify(payload))
174:     }
175:   }
176: 
177:   private setState(state: ConnectionState): void {
178:     this.handlers.onStateChange(state)
179:   }
180: }

</content>
