1: /**
2:  * Client-side voice activity detection (VAD) contract.
3:  *
4:  * The Silero VAD provider runs in a Web Worker so inference never blocks the
5:  * audio streaming path. The worklet keeps producing PCM16 chunks for the
6:  * network while the VAD worker consumes the same 16 kHz stream and emits the
7:  * five lifecycle events below.
8:  */
9: 
10: export type VADEventType =
11:   | "speech_started"
12:   | "speaking"
13:   | "silence_started"
14:   | "silence_detected"
15:   | "speech_resumed"
16: 
17: export interface VADEvent {
18:   type: VADEventType
19:   /** Epoch ms when the transition was detected. */
20:   timestamp: number
21:   /** Silero speech probability at the moment of the event (0..1). */
22:   probability: number
23:   /** Measured silence gap, set on `silence_detected`. */
24:   durationMs?: number
25: }
26: 
27: export type VADStatus =
28:   | "idle"
29:   | "loading"
30:   | "speaking"
31:   | "silence"
32:   | "error"
33: 
34: export interface VADConfig {
35:   /** ASR rate the worklet resamples to before feeding VAD. */
36:   sampleRate: number
37:   /** Silero processes fixed 30 ms windows: 512 samples @ 16 kHz. */
38:   windowSize: number
39:   /**
40:    * Silero v5 expects 64 samples of the previous window prepended to the
41:    * current one (context). The real model input is windowSize + contextSize.
42:    */
43:   contextSize: number
44:   /** Probability at which speech is considered to have started (0..1). */
45:   speechProbThreshold: number
46:   /**
47:    * After this much silence, `silence_started` fires and the UI shows
48:    * "Silence detected" even though the utterance may still be ongoing.
49:    */
50:   hangoverMs: number
51:   /**
52:    * An utterance boundary: once silence exceeds this (measured from the last
53:    * speech frame), `silence_detected` fires and later speech starts a new
54:    * utterance. Short pauses (e.g. 100 ms) never get this far.
55:    */
56:   silenceThresholdMs: number
57:   /** Cadence of the `speaking` heartbeat while speech is active. */
58:   speakingHeartbeatMs: number
59:   /** Same-origin model path (provisioned by scripts/setup-vad.mjs). */
60:   modelUrl: string
61:   /** CDN fallbacks tried when the same-origin model is missing. */
62:   modelFallbackUrls: string[]
63: }
64: 
65: export const DEFAULT_VAD_CONFIG: VADConfig = {
66:   sampleRate: 16_000,
67:   windowSize: 512,
68:   contextSize: 64,
69:   speechProbThreshold: 0.5,
70:   hangoverMs: 300,
71:   silenceThresholdMs: 600,
72:   speakingHeartbeatMs: 200,
73:   modelUrl: "/models/silero_vad.onnx",
74:   modelFallbackUrls: [
75:     "https://github.com/snakers4/silero-vad/raw/master/src/silero_vad/data/silero_vad.onnx",
76:     "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/snakers4/silero-vad/master/src/silero_vad/data/silero_vad.onnx",
77:   ],
78: }
79: 
80: export interface VADProvider {
81:   /** Begin (or resume) loading the model. Never blocks callers. */
82:   init(): Promise<void>
83:   /** Begin VAD processing of frames forwarded via processFrame(). */
84:   start(): Promise<void>
85:   /** Stop VAD processing and reset the internal state machine. */
86:   stop(): Promise<void>
87:   /** Feed one contiguous Float32 window (windowSize samples @ sampleRate). */
88:   processFrame(samples: Float32Array): void
89:   /** Subscribe to VAD lifecycle events. Returns an unsubscribe function. */
90:   onEvent(callback: (event: VADEvent) => void): () => void
91:   /** Subscribe to provider status changes (loading/speaking/...). */

    found = []

## Assistant (Build · Big Pickle · 9.0s)

_Thinking:_

Two issues:

1. `recorder.requests == []` — the MockTransport is NOT calling my `_Recorder.handle_request`. Wait — I passed `_Recorder` as transport to AsyncClient. httpx checks `isinstance(transport, MockTransport)` and calls `handle_request`. My `_Recorder.__init__` calls `super().__init__(handler)` then sets `self.handler = handler`. And overrides handle_request. So handle_request should be called. But requests is empty and translate returned "Hola" — so the request WAS handled (result success). So handle_request WAS invoked but `self.requests` stayed empty? That means a DIFFERENT instance handled it, or `self.requests.append` happened on a different object...

Ah — MockTransport is async; httpx AsyncClient calls `await transport.handle_async_request(...)`. In newer httpx, MockTransport has `handle_async_request` and sync `handle_request`. When used with AsyncClient, httpx uses `handle_async_request`. MockTransport.handle_async_request is an async method that calls `self.handler(request)`. My override `handle_request` (sync) may NOT be called in async mode!

So for AsyncClient, I should override `handle_async_request`. Actually in httpx, `MockTransport` when used via async calls `handle_async_request`, which is defined to call `self.handler`. My override of the sync `handle_request` isn't used. That's why requests stayed empty but handler worked.

Fix: override `handle_async_request` as async. In httpx, `MockTransport.handle_async_request(request)` is async and returns `await self.handler(request)` essentially. Let me define:

```python
class _Recorder(httpx.MockTransport):
    def __init__(self, handler):
        super().__init__(handler)
        self.requests = []
    async def handle_async_request(self, request):
        self.requests.append(request)
        return await super().handle_async_request(request)
```

`super().handle_async_request(request)` in MockTransport: `return await self.handler(request)`. Yes.

2. `health_check` is async (it's `async def health_check` in cloud_provider). I need `await provider.health_check()`. My test treated it sync. Fix to await.

<content>
1: # Client-side Voice Activity Detection (Silero VAD)
2: 
3: Voice activity detection tells the app when the user is speaking and when they
4: have stopped. It runs **entirely in the browser** so the latency between "user
5: stops talking" and "we can finalize the utterance" is a few milliseconds
6: instead of a network round-trip.
7: 
8: ```
9: Microphone ──▶ AudioWorklet ──┬──▶ 16 kHz PCM16 ──▶ WebSocket ──▶ backend
10: (pcmCaptureWorklet.js)        │
11:                               └──▶ 512-sample Float32 windows
12:                                    └──▶ VAD Worker ──▶ speech/silence events
13:                                         (onnxruntime-web WASM + Silero v5)
14: ```
15: 
16: VAD inference lives in a **Web Worker**, not the AudioWorklet, so classification
17: never competes with the real-time audio graph and never blocks the streaming
18: path. Streaming and VAD consume the same 16 kHz resampled stream concurrently.
19: 
20: ## Events
21: 
22: | Event | When it fires | UI |
23: |---|---|---|
24: | `speech_started` | probability crosses the threshold from silence | ● Speaking |
25: | `speaking` | heartbeat while speech stays active (default every 200 ms) | ● Speaking |
26: | `silence_started` | speech dropped below threshold for the hangover (300 ms) | ○ Silence detected |
27: | `silence_detected` | silence exceeds the utterance threshold (default 600 ms) | ○ Silence detected |
28: | `speech_resumed` | speech returns while the utterance is still "pending" | ● Speaking |
29: 
30: Because `silence_detected` requires the silence to exceed the configured
31: threshold measured from the *last* speech frame:
32: 
33: - a **100 ms pause** ("Hello … World") produces **no boundary** — the state
34:   machine stays in `speaking` (below the 300 ms hangover) and `speech_resumed`
35:   is never needed;
36: - a **600 ms pause** produces `silence_detected` (with `duration_ms: 600`),
37:   which the backend records (`session.last_vad_event`) and can later use to
38:   force a clean utterance boundary for ASR finalization.
39: 
40: ### Hysteresis
41: 
42: Silero probabilities swing frame to frame, so the state machine uses two
43: thresholds (the same rule as Silero's reference `VADIterator`):
44: 
45: - **onset** — `speechProbThreshold` (default `0.5`) to *enter* speech;
46: - **release** — `speechProbThreshold - 0.15` to *leave* it.
47: 
48: Noise measures p≈0.01–0.02, silence p<0.01, and real speech p up to 1.0, so
49: the default threshold is well separated from both.
50: 
51: ## Configuration
52: 
53: Configurable at runtime (Settings → *Voice activity detection*), live:
54: 
55: | Setting | Default | Effect |
56: |---|---|---|
57: | Silence threshold (`silenceThresholdMs`) | 600 ms | Pauses longer than this end the utterance; shorter ones keep it. Range 100–1500 ms. |
58: | Speech sensitivity (`speechProbThreshold`) | 0.50 | Lower ⇒ catches quieter speech but risks noise triggers. Range 0.30–0.90. |
59: 
60: Fixed by design: `windowSize` 512 samples (30 ms @ 16 kHz), `contextSize` 64,
61: `hangoverMs` 300, `speakingHeartbeatMs` 200. Full defaults live in
62: `frontend/src/providers/vad/types.ts` (`DEFAULT_VAD_CONFIG`).
63: 
64: ## Model loading
65: 
66: 1. `frontend/scripts/setup-vad.mjs` (run by `npm run vad:setup`, and
67:    automatically by `predev`/`prebuild`) provisions:
68:    - `frontend/public/models/silero_vad.onnx` — Silero VAD **v5**
69:      (`https://github.com/snakers4/silero-vad`), ~2.3 MB, downloaded once;
70:    - `frontend/public/vendor/onnx/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.{mjs,wasm}` — the
71:      onnxruntime-web loader + WASM (~13.5 MB), copied from
72:      `node_modules/onnxruntime-web/dist/` (no network).
73: 2. At runtime the VAD worker sets `ort.env.wasm.wasmPaths = "/vendor/onnx/"`,
74:    fetches the model (same-origin first, CDN fallbacks after), and creates an
75:    `InferenceSession`. If the model file is missing, the app falls back to the
76:    CDN copy; if that also fails, the VAD indicator shows *VAD error* and the
77:    UI falls back to the worklet's RMS activity check.
78: 
79: ### Model contract (Silero VAD v5)
80: 
81: ```
82: input  : float32 [1, 576]   ← 64 context samples + 512 window (16 kHz)
83: state  : float32 [2, 1, 128] ← recurrent state, zeros to start
84: sr     : int64  [1]          ← 16000
85: output : float32 [1, 1]      ← speech probability
86: stateN : float32 [2, 1, 128] ← state for the next window
87: ```
88: 
89: The 64-sample context (the tail of the previous window, or zeros) is required;
90: feeding 512 samples alone produces unreliable probabilities. Both the Python
91: and JavaScript probes reproduced identical results on the reference clip
92: (1452/1875 windows ≥ 0.5, p max 1.0).
93: 
94: ## Browser compatibility
95: 
96: - Requires `AudioWorklet` (Chrome 66+, Edge, Firefox 76+, Safari 14.1+).
97: - Requires WebAssembly + **SharedArrayBuffer-compatible threads**, which all
98:   evergreen browsers provide.
99: - The worker runs **single-threaded** by default
100:   (`ort.env.wasm.numThreads = 1`), which works without cross-origin isolation.
101: - For multi-threaded WASM inference, the hosting page must opt into cross-origin
102:   isolation (`Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` and
103:   `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp`). This app does not require it;
104:   VAD is cheap (~1 ms per 30 ms window) so a single thread is sufficient.
105: - Web Workers (`type: "module"`) require a secure context — fine on
106:   `localhost` in development and on HTTPS in production.
107: 
108: ## Performance
109: 
110: | Step | Cost |
111: |---|---|
112: | Worklet resample + Float32 window (512 samples) | negligible, real-time thread |
113: | Worker inference (WASM, single thread) | ~1 ms per 30 ms window, off main thread |
114: | WASM fetch + session creation | ~1–2 s one-time, overlapped with streaming start |
115: | Frames during model load | buffered (up to ~4.5 s) in the worker, replayed in order |
116: 
117: The VAD worker never blocks `sendAudio`: the AudioWorklet posts PCM16 chunks
118: and VAD windows as independent messages, and `session.run()` is serialized on a
119: promise chain in the worker so frames are processed in order without ever
120: back-pressuring the audio graph.
121: 
122: ## Manual test checklist (requires a real microphone)
123: 
124: 1. `cd backend && uv run uvicorn app.main:app` and
125:    `cd frontend && npm run dev`.
126: 2. Open `http://localhost:5173`, allow the microphone, press **Start**.
127: 3. In the header: *VAD loading…* appears briefly, then *Listening*.
128: 4. Speak: the indicator flips to **● Speaking** and the session status to
129:    *Speaking*. Stop: after ~300 ms it shows **○ Silence detected**.
130: 5. Say "Hello" then pause ~100 ms then "world" — the utterance must **not**
131:    end (status returns to *Speaking*, no `silence_detected`).
132: 6. Speak a sentence and stay silent ~600 ms — the VAD indicator stays at
133:    *Silence detected* and a `vad_event` with `event: "silence_detected"` is
134:    logged by the backend (visible in the backend console at debug level).
135: 7. Settings → *Voice activity detection*: raise/lower the silence threshold
136:    and confirm the boundary behaviour changes immediately.
137: 8. Diagnostics panel (dev only): *VAD model*, *VAD probability* (should climb
138:    above 0.5 while speaking, drop below 0.1 in silence), *VAD silence threshold*.
139: 
140: ## Files
141: 
142: - `frontend/src/providers/vad/types.ts` — events, config, provider interface.
143: - `frontend/src/providers/vad/sileroVADWorker.ts` — inference + state machine.
144: - `frontend/src/providers/vad/sileroVADProvider.ts` — main-thread wrapper.
145: - `frontend/src/audio/pcmCaptureWorklet.js` — resample/stream + VAD windows.
146: - `frontend/src/hooks/useAudioCapture.ts` — VAD wiring in the capture hook.
147: - `frontend/src/hooks/useTranslatorSession.ts` — VAD events → status + backend.
148: - `frontend/scripts/setup-vad.mjs` — asset provisioning.
149: - `backend/app/websocket/translate_stream.py` — `vad_event` handling.
150: - `backend/app/models/schemas.py` — `VADEventMessage` protocol model.

(End of file - total 150 lines)
</content>

{
  "content": "# Translation: hybrid cloud → NLLB-200 fallback\n\nTranslation is handled by a small provider family behind the\n`TranslationProvider` interface. The pipeline calls **one** abstraction; it\nnever branches on provider type or on language pairs.\n\n```\nTranscript final\n     │  (finalized utterances only)\n     ▼\nTranslationQueue (per-session, ordered)\n     │\n     ▼\nHybridTranslationProvider\n     ├─ CloudTranslationProvider  ── succeeds ──► cloud text\n     │     (Google Cloud Translation v2 REST, low latency)\n     └─ on TranslationError ▼\n        NLLBTranslationProvider ── succeeds ──► NLLB text (provider=\"nllb\")\n        (NLLB-200 distilled 600M, offline)\n            └─ also fails ──► error event \"translation_failed\" (non-fatal)\n```\n\nRules that hold by design:\n\n- **Cloud first.** The cloud API is the primary, low-latency path.\n- **NLLB fallback on failure.** Any `TranslationError` from the cloud provider\n  (missing key, network error, HTTP 4xx/5xx, malformed body) triggers the\n  offline provider for that utterance.\n- **Never fail the meeting.** A transient translation failure is reported to\n  the client as an `error` event with code `translation_failed`; the session\n  and all subsequent utterances keep running. The frontend treats that code\n  as non-fatal.\n- **Finalized utterances only.** Partials stream straight to the client and\n  are never queued for translation.\n- **Provider-specific codes are resolved centrally** (see below); the\n  pipeline contains zero hardcoded language-pair conditionals.\n- **No LLM as translator.** The models are not used for translation; the LLM\n  is reserved for transcript refinement (see `docs/refinement.md` if present).\n\n## Provider modes\n\nSelected by `TRANSLATION_PROVIDER` (`translation_provider` setting):\n\n| Mode | Behavior |\n|---|---|\n| `hybrid` (default) | cloud first, NLLB-200 fallback |\n| `cloud` | cloud only; failures surface as `translation_failed` |\n| `nllb` | NLLB-200 only |\n\nThe factory `create_translation_provider()` in\n`backend/app/services/translation/__init__.py` reads the setting and also\napplies the `TRANSLATION_EXTRA_LANGUAGES` registry entries before returning.\n\n## Central language registry\n\n`backend/app/services/translation/languages.py` is the single source of truth.\nEach `Language` entry carries:\n\n- `iso_code` — canonical code used across the app (`en`, `hi`, `ta`, …);\n- `display_name` — human-readable name;\n- `cloud_code` — cloud API code (defaults to `iso_code`);\n- `nllb_code` — NLLB-200 FLORES-200 token (`hin_Deva`, `tam_Taml`, …).\n\nResolution helpers:\n\n- `cloud_code(\"auto\")` → `\"auto\"` (cloud performs source detection when the\n  `source` param is omitted).\n- `nllb_code(\"auto\")` → `TranslationError(\"unsupported_language\")` — NLLB has\n  no language detection.\n\nBuilt-in languages: en, hi, ta, te, ml, kn, es, fr, de, pt, ja, ko, zh, ar, ru.\n\nAdd a language in three ways:\n1. edit `LANGUAGES` in `languages.py`;\n2. `register_language(Language(...))` at runtime;\n3. set `TRANSLATION_EXTRA_LANGUAGES` (JSON list) in `.env`.\n\n```\nTRANSLATION_EXTRA_LANGUAGES=[{\"iso_code\":\"mr\",\"display_name\":\"Marathi\",\"nllb_code\":\"mar_Deva\"}]\n```\n\n## Cloud provider\n\n`backend/app/services/translation/cloud_provider.py` calls the Google Cloud\nTranslation v2 REST endpoint directly with httpx (no SDK):\n\n- POST `{cloud_translation_endpoint}` (default\n  `https://translation.googleapis.com/language/translate/v2`)\n- `?key={CLOUD_TRANSLATION_API_KEY}`,\n  body `{\"q\": text, \"target\": cloud_code, \"format\": \"text\"[, \"source\": …]}`\n- `source` omitted when the source language is `auto`.\n\nFailure codes (all `TranslationError`):\n\n| Code | Trigger |\n|---|---|\n| `cloud_config` | provider name ≠ `google`, or API key missing |\n| `cloud_connection` | httpx network/transport error |\n| `cloud_translation_error` | HTTP ≥ 400 or malformed response body |\n\nBlank text short-circuits to an empty translation without a network call.\n`cloud_translation_provider_name` accepts `google`, `deepl`, `azure` but only\n`google` is wired; anything else fails with `cloud_config`.\n\n## NLLB provider\n\n`backend/app/services/translation/nllb_provider.py` loads\n`facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M` (default, overridable via `NLLB_MODEL_NAME`)\n**lazily** on first use, off the event loop:\n\n- `warm_up()` / first `translate()` acquire an `asyncio.Lock` and load the\n  model in a thread (`asyncio.to_thread(self._load_model)`);\n- generation runs in `_translate_engine(...)` in a thread with\n  `forced_bos_token_id` set to the target FLORES token;\n- if torch/transformers are missing (`ImportError`) or the model fails to\n  load, `translate()` raises `TranslationError(\"nllb_model_unavailable\")`.\n\n**Install note.** The heavy dependencies (torch, transformers, sentencepiece)\nlive in the `offline` extra and only install cleanly on Python 3.11/3.12:\n\n```\nuv sync --extra offline   # on a Python 3.11/3.12 interpreter\n```\n\nOn the current Python 3.14 runtime the provider is exercised entirely through\ntests that monkeypatch `_load_model` / `_translate_engine`; a real model run\nrequires the `offline` extra.\n\n## Transport integration\n\n`backend/app/websocket/translate_stream.py`:\n\n- `Session.translation_queue` — ordered `asyncio.Queue` of\n  `(segment_id, text)` pairs for finalized utterances;\n- `Session.translation_task` — one worker per session, started in\n  `apply_config`, torn down in `stop()`/re-configuration;\n- `_run_asr` enqueues only `segment.is_final` items (after the transcript +\n  `asr_ms` latency events are sent);\n- `_run_translation` sends a `translation` event plus a `latency` event with\n  `translation_ms`; a failure sends `error { code: \"translation_failed\" }`\n  and moves on.\n\nPer-segment client event order:\n\n```\npartial_transcript → final_transcript → latency(asr_ms) → translation → latency(translation_ms)\n```\n\n## Latency measurement\n\n`_run_translation` times the provider call with `time.monotonic()` and reports\n`translation_ms` in a `latency` event. The frontend `LatencyIndicator` shows\nthe most specific metric available: `translation_ms` → `asr_ms` →\n`end_to_end_ms`.\n\n## Frontend\n\n- `useTranslatorSession.ts` — `translation` events update the latest +\n  history panels; `error` with code `translation_failed` is **non-fatal**\n  (session status unchanged).\n- `LatencyIndicator.tsx` — dev-only pill showing Translation/ASR latency.\n\n## Testing\n\n- `tests/test_languages.py` — registry mapping, `auto` semantics, unknown\n  language rejection, runtime registration.\n- `tests/test_translation_providers.py` — cloud provider against\n  `httpx.MockTransport` (no network), NLLB via monkeypatched\n  `_load_model`/`_translate_engine`, hybrid fallback and dual-failure, factory\n  modes.\n- `tests/test_websocket.py` — finals-only translation, in-order delivery,\n  per-session languages, non-fatal `translation_failed`, `translation_ms`.\n\n## Files\n\n- `backend/app/services/translation/base.py` — `TranslationProvider`,\n  `TranslationError`.\n- `backend/app/services/translation/languages.py` — registry.\n- `backend/app/services/translation/cloud_provider.py`, `nllb_provider.py`,\n  `hybrid_provider.py`, `__init__.py` (factory).\n- `backend/app/websocket/translate_stream.py` — queue/worker integration.\n- `backend/app/config.py` — `translation_provider`, `cloud_translation_*`,\n  `translation_extra_languages`, `nllb_*` settings.\n- `frontend/src/hooks/useTranslatorSession.ts`,\n  `frontend/src/components/LatencyIndicator/LatencyIndicator.tsx`.\n",

<content>
1: # Real-Time Translator
2: 
3: A real-time, multilingual speech translator for online meetings (Zoom, Google Meet, etc.).
4: Streams live speech to text, translates it, and displays translated captions with
5: minimal latency — with silence detection used to produce clean sentence boundaries
6: and punctuation.
7: 
8: > **Status:** client-side Silero VAD is implemented (Phase 1.5) and the backend
9: > now streams live transcripts through **Deepgram streaming ASR** (Phase 1):
10: > interim/final results, punctuation + smart formatting, multilingual /
11: > language-detection, client-silence-driven utterance finalization, automatic
12: > reconnects, and measured ASR latency. The backend boots, serves `/health`, and
13: > passes 37 tests (transport + a Deepgram provider suite against a fake
14: > Deepgram server); the frontend typechecks, lints, builds, and renders
15: > real-time partial/final transcripts that freeze on finalization. Translation
16: > and LLM refinement are the remaining build phases — see `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md`.
17: 
18: ## What this is
19: 
20: - **ASR:** Deepgram Streaming API (default), behind an `ASRProvider` interface.
21: - **Translation:** hybrid — a low-latency cloud provider by default, with NLLB-200
22:   as an offline/fallback provider, behind a `TranslationProvider` interface.
23: - **VAD (silence detection):** client-side Silero VAD running in an AudioWorklet,
24:   so silence detection never adds server round-trip latency.
25: - **LLM refinement:** an async, post-hoc pass that improves punctuation,
26:   capitalization, obvious ASR errors, and contextual terminology — it runs
27:   **after** an utterance is finalized and is never on the latency-critical path.
28: 
29: ## Project structure
30: 
31: ```
32: real-time-translator/
33: ├── frontend/          React + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind UI
34: │   └── src/
35: │       ├── components/  LanguageSelector, AudioControls, ConnectionStatus,
36: │       │                LatencyIndicator, ErrorBanner, TranscriptPanel,
37: │       │                TranslationPanel
38: │       ├── hooks/       useTranslatorSession, useAudioCapture
39: │       ├── providers/   vad/ (VADProvider interface + SileroVADProvider stub)
40: │       ├── lib/         wsClient.ts (TranslatorClient WebSocket wrapper)
41: │       ├── types/       shared types mirroring backend schemas
42: │       └── styles/      Tailwind entrypoint
43: ├── backend/           FastAPI + asyncio + WebSocket pipeline
44: │   ├── app/             main.py, config.py, websocket/, services/ (asr,
45: │   │                    translation, vad, llm), models/, utils/
46: │   └── tests/           pytest suite (health, config, websocket, VAD)
47: ├── docs/              Supplementary docs
48: ├── tests/             Cross-cutting / integration tests (root level)
49: ├── .env.example       All environment variables, documented
50: ├── .gitignore
51: ├── README.md          You are here
52: ├── ARCHITECTURE.md    System design, data flow, provider abstractions
53: └── DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md  Phased build-out plan and current status
54: ```
55: 
56: See `ARCHITECTURE.md` for the full system design and `backend/app/services/*`
57: for the provider interfaces (`ASRProvider`, `TranslationProvider`, `LLMProvider`)
58: that keep business logic decoupled from any single vendor.
59: 
60: ## Prerequisites
61: 
62: - Python 3.11+ (backend core). Tested on 3.14.
63: - Node.js 20+ and npm (frontend).
64: - [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for Python dependency management (recommended),
65:   or plain `pip` + `venv`.
66: - API keys for whichever providers you enable (Deepgram, a cloud translation
67:   provider, an LLM provider) — see `.env.example`. None are required to run the
68:   scaffold: `/health` and the frontend shell need no external providers.
69: 
70: > Python version note: the backend pins `requires-python = ">=3.11"`. The core
71: > dependencies run fine on 3.14. Only the *offline* extra (`torch`,
72: > `transformers`, for NLLB-200) is constrained to 3.11/3.12 because those
73: > packages do not yet ship stable wheels for 3.14 — install it with
74: > `uv sync --extra offline` only if you need the offline fallback.
75: 
76: ## Getting started
77: 
78: ### Backend
79: 
80: ```bash
81: cd backend
82: uv sync                         # creates/updates .venv and installs deps
83: cp ../.env.example .env         # then fill in DEEPGRAM_API_KEY etc. (optional)
84: uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
85: ```
86: 
87: Verify it's up:
88: 
89: ```bash
90: curl http://localhost:8000/health
91: # {"status":"ok","env":"development","asr_provider":"deepgram","translation_provider":"cloud"}
92: ```
93: 
94: ### Frontend
95: 
96: ```bash
97: cd frontend
98: npm install
99: npm run dev
100: ```
101: 
102: Open the URL Vite prints (default `http://localhost:5173`). The Vite dev server
103: proxies `/api` and `/ws` to `http://localhost:8000` (see `frontend/vite.config.ts`),
104: so the frontend and backend can be developed independently.
105: 
106: ### Running checks
107: 
108: ```bash
109: # Backend: lint + tests
110: cd backend && uv run ruff check .
111: cd backend && uv run pytest
112: 
113: # Frontend: lint + typecheck + build
114: cd frontend && npm run lint
115: cd frontend && npm run typecheck
116: cd frontend && npm run build
117: ```
118: 
119: ## Design principles
120: 
121: 1. **Provider abstractions everywhere.** `ASRProvider`, `TranslationProvider`,
122:    `LLMProvider`, and a client-side `VADProvider` mean no business logic is
123:    tightly coupled to Deepgram, a specific translation API, or a specific LLM.
124: 2. **Latency-critical path stays lean.** ASR → translation → display is the hot
125:    path. LLM refinement is strictly async and only ever *improves* text already
126:    shown to the user — it never blocks it.
127: 3. **Silence is signal.** Client-side VAD silence events double as endpointing
128:    hints, giving cleaner sentence boundaries and punctuation than relying on
129:    ASR endpointing alone.
130: 4. **UI needs no manual.** Two panels (original / translation), one big
131:    start/stop control, obvious connection and latency indicators.
132: 
133: ## Roadmap
134: 
135: See `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md` for the phased plan, from this scaffold through
136: production hardening and system/meeting-audio ingestion.

(End of file - total 136 lines)
</content>
```

<content>
1: # Architecture
2: 
3: ## 1. Goals and constraints
4: 
5: - **Low latency end-to-end.** Speech must appear as translated captions within a
6:   few hundred milliseconds, not seconds.
7: - **Provider independence.** Deepgram, the cloud translation API, NLLB-200, and
8:   the LLM refinement provider must all be swappable without touching pipeline
9:   or UI code. This is enforced with abstract provider interfaces.
10: - **Correctness improves without blocking speed.** Punctuation/terminology
11:   refinement is valuable but must never sit on the hot path.
12: - **Silence is a first-class signal**, not just "no audio" — it's used both to
13:   save bandwidth/compute and to produce clean sentence boundaries.
14: - **Extensible to meeting audio.** The pipeline should not assume "microphone"
15:   as the only audio source; system/meeting audio capture is a planned input,
16:   not an architectural afterthought.
17: 
18: ## 2. High-level data flow
19: 
20: ```
21: ┌─────────────┐   PCM frames    ┌──────────────────┐
22: │  Microphone /│ ───────────────▶│  Silero VAD       │  (AudioWorklet, client-side)
23: │  meeting audio│                │  speech/silence   │
24: └─────────────┘                 └─────────┬─────────┘
25:                                            │ speech_start / speech_end events
26:                                            ▼
27:                               ┌────────────────────────┐
28:                               │  Audio capture pipeline  │  (client-side)
29:                               │  getUserMedia → Worklet  │
30:                               └────────────┬─────────────┘
31:                                            │ 16kHz PCM frames + silence events
32:                                            ▼  (WebSocket, binary + JSON control)
33:                               ┌────────────────────────┐
34:                                │   FastAPI WS endpoint    │  backend/app/websocket
35:                                │   /ws/translate           │
36:                               └────────────┬─────────────┘
37:                                            │
38:                           ┌────────────────┼────────────────┐
39:                           ▼                                   ▼
40:               ┌─────────────────────┐             notify_silence() hints
41:               │   ASRProvider         │◀───────────────────────────────┐
42:               │   (Deepgram default)  │                                 │
43:               └───────────┬───────────┘                                 │
44:                           │ partial + final TranscriptSegment            │
45:                           ▼                                              │
46:               ┌─────────────────────┐                                   │
47:               │  TranslationProvider  │  hybrid: cloud (default) ────────┘
48:               │  cloud / NLLB          │  or NLLB-200 (fallback/offline)
49:               └───────────┬───────────┘
50:                           │ partial + final TranslationSegment
51:                           ▼
52:               ┌─────────────────────┐        (fire-and-forget, async)
53:               │  Client (React UI)    │◀────────────┐
54:               │  transcript + captions │             │
55:               └───────────┬───────────┘             │
56:                           │ final segment id          │
57:                           ▼                            │
58:               ┌─────────────────────┐                 │
59:               │   LLMProvider          │────────────────┘
60:               │   async refinement pass │  REFINEMENT event, replaces
61:               └─────────────────────┘  displayed text in place, non-blocking
62: ```
63: 
64: Key point: **the LLM box is not in the request/response chain that produces the
65: first visible caption.** It's triggered after a segment is finalized, runs in
66: a background asyncio task, and pushes a correction later via a separate
67: `refinement` WebSocket event. The UI already has *something* on screen; the
68: refinement just makes it better.
69: 
70: ## 3. Provider abstractions
71: 
72: All providers are ABCs so the pipeline/orchestrator and the UI depend only on
73: interfaces, never concrete vendors.
74: 
75: ### `ASRProvider` (`backend/app/services/asr/base.py`)
76: 
77: ```
78: connect(sample_rate, encoding, language) -> None
79: send_audio(chunk: bytes) -> None
80: notify_silence(duration_ms: int) -> None
81: stream() -> AsyncIterator[TranscriptSegment]
82: close() -> None
83: ```
84: 
85: `DeepgramASRProvider` is the default implementation. `notify_silence` maps to
86: Deepgram's endpointing/finalize controls, letting client-detected silence force
87: a clean utterance boundary rather than waiting on server-side heuristics alone.
88: 
89: ### `TranslationProvider` (`backend/app/services/translation/base.py`)
90: 
91: ```
92: translate(segment_id, text, source_language, target_language, is_final) -> TranslationSegment
93: warm_up() -> None            # optional: load models / open connections
94: health_check() -> bool       # optional: used by the hybrid router
95: ```
96: 
97: Two implementations:
98: - `CloudTranslationProvider` — default. Wraps a cloud translation API
99:   (Google / DeepL / Azure, selected via config) for lowest latency.
100: - `NLLBTranslationProvider` — offline fallback using the NLLB-200 model,
101:   used when the cloud provider's `health_check()` fails, when explicitly
102:   configured for offline operation, or for languages the cloud provider
103:   doesn't cover well.
104: 
105: A thin **hybrid router** (planned in `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md` Phase 2) selects
106: between them per request based on `health_check()` and configuration, so
107: callers just call "the" `TranslationProvider`.
108: 
109: ### `LLMProvider` (`backend/app/services/llm/base.py`)
110: 
111: ```
112: refine(segment_id, text, language, context) -> RefinementResult
113: ```
114: 
115: `LLMRefinementProvider` is the default implementation. `context` is a short
116: window of recent finalized segments so terminology stays consistent across an
117: utterance or meeting (e.g. a company/product name transcribed inconsistently).
118: 
119: ### `VADProvider` (frontend: `frontend/src/providers/vad/types.ts`)
120: 
121: VAD runs **client-side** for latency reasons (a round-trip to the server just
122: to learn "the user stopped talking" would defeat the purpose). The interface:
123: 
124: ```
125: init() -> Promise<void>
126: start(stream: MediaStream) -> Promise<void>
127: stop() -> Promise<void>
128: onEvent(callback: (event: VADEvent) => void) -> void
129: ```
130: 
131: `SileroVADProvider` runs the Silero VAD model inside an `AudioWorkletProcessor`
132: so classification happens off the main thread, frame-by-frame, with no
133: network round trip. `speech_start`/`speech_end` events are turned into
134: `silence` WebSocket messages the backend forwards to the ASR provider as
135: endpointing hints.
136: 
137: The backend also defines a `SilenceDetector` helper
138: (`backend/app/services/vad/base.py`) that turns raw silence-duration reports
139: into a "should this finalize the utterance?" decision, using two tunables:
140: - `SILENCE_FINALIZE_MS` — how much silence implies "sentence is over".
141: - `SILENCE_MIN_SPEECH_MS` — minimum preceding speech to avoid false triggers
142:   from breath sounds / noise.
143: 
144: ## 4. Why VAD is client-side but the interface lives on both sides
145: 
146: Silero VAD executes in the browser for latency. But the *concept* of "was this
147: gap in audio significant enough to be a sentence boundary" is also useful
148: server-side (e.g. if audio ever arrives from a source without a client
149: worklet — a recorded meeting file, or server-side capture of meeting audio).
150: That's why there's a `VADProvider` interface on the frontend for the live
151: capture path, and a separate `SilenceDetector`/`VADProvider` on the backend for
152: interpreting silence signals and, later, for any server-side VAD fallback —
153: without changing how the ASR/translation pipeline consumes "silence happened
154: here" events.
155: 
156: ## 5. WebSocket protocol
157: 
158: Single endpoint: `ws://<backend>/ws/translate`. See
159: `backend/app/models/schemas.py` for exact payloads. Every message is a JSON
160: envelope of the form `{"type": "<message>", ...fields}`; audio frames travel as
161: raw binary WebSocket messages rather than base64-encoded JSON.
162: 
163: **Client → Server**
164: | Message | Shape |
165: |---|---|
166: | Start session | `{"type": "start_session", "session_id"?: str}` |
167: | Session configuration | `{"type": "session_configuration", session_id, source_language, target_language, audio_source, sample_rate?, encoding?}` |
168: | Audio | binary WebSocket frame (raw PCM16 or Opus) |
169: | Audio chunk (control) | `{"type": "audio_chunk", "session_id": str}` |
170: | Stop session | `{"type": "stop_session", "session_id": str}` |
171: 
172: **Server → Client**
173: | Message | Shape |
174: |---|---|
175: | Session started | `{"type": "session_started", session_id, configuration}` |
176: | Speech lifecycle | `{"type": "speech_started" \| "silence_detected" \| "speech_resumed", session_id, timestamp_ms, duration_ms?}` |
177: | Partial/final transcript | `{"type": "partial_transcript" \| "final_transcript", session_id, ...TranscriptEvent}` |
178: | Translation | `{"type": "translation", session_id, ...TranslationEvent}` |
179: | Async refinement | `{"type": "refined_transcript", session_id, segment_id, refined_text, changed}` |
180: | Latency report | `{"type": "latency", session_id, segment_id, asr_ms, translation_ms, end_to_end_ms}` |
181: | Error | `{"type": "error", code, message, session_id?}` |
182: | Session stopped | `{"type": "session_stopped", session_id, reason}` |
183: 
184: ## 6. Frontend structure
185: 
186: ```
187: frontend/src/
188: ├── components/         one folder per reusable UI piece (own file + index.ts)
189: │   ├── LanguageSelector/
190: │   ├── AudioControls/
191: │   ├── ConnectionStatus/
192: │   ├── LatencyIndicator/
193: │   ├── ErrorBanner/
194: │   ├── TranscriptPanel/
195: │   └── TranslationPanel/
196: ├── hooks/
197: │   ├── useTranslatorSession.ts   orchestrates connection + pipeline state
198: │   └── useAudioCapture.ts        getUserMedia + AudioWorklet plumbing
199: ├── providers/
200: │   └── vad/                      VADProvider interface + SileroVADProvider
201: ├── lib/
202: │   └── wsClient.ts                thin WebSocket transport (TranslatorClient)
203: ├── types/                         shared types mirroring backend schemas
204: ├── styles/                        Tailwind entrypoint
205: ├── App.tsx                        UI shell: selectors, controls, two panels
206: └── main.tsx
207: ```
208: 
209: `useTranslatorSession` is the single seam between UI and networking/audio —
210: components never touch `WebSocket` or `MediaStream` directly, which keeps the
211: UI layer trivial to test and restyle.
212: 
213: ## 7. Backend structure
214: 
215: ```
216: backend/app/
217: ├── main.py              FastAPI app: CORS, router mounting, /health
218: ├── config.py             pydantic-settings Settings, env-driven
219: ├── websocket/
220: │   └── translate_stream.py  /ws/translate transport layer (thin) + SessionManager
221: ├── services/
222: │   ├── asr/               ASRProvider + DeepgramASRProvider
223: │   ├── translation/        TranslationProvider + Cloud/NLLB implementations
224: │   ├── vad/                 VADProvider + SilenceDetector
225: │   └── llm/                  LLMProvider + LLMRefinementProvider
226: ├── models/
227: │   └── schemas.py          shared Pydantic models (WS + internal)
228: └── utils/
229:     └── logging.py           structlog setup
230: ```
231: 
232: Notice `websocket/translate_stream.py` stays thin on purpose — it's transport, not
233: orchestration. As Phase 2 (see `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md`) lands, a
234: `PipelineOrchestrator` (or similar) will sit between the transport layer and
235: the providers, owning per-session state, provider selection, and the async
236: refinement dispatch — keeping the WebSocket handler itself simple regardless
237: of how complex the pipeline gets.
238: 
239: ## 8. Path to meeting/system audio
240: 
241: Today's design already generalizes past "microphone": the WebSocket protocol
242: and `ASRProvider` interface don't care where PCM frames come from. Consuming
243: Zoom/Meet system audio is a matter of adding a capture source (e.g. a
244: platform-level loopback capture, a meeting-bot integration, or a browser tab
245: audio capture) that feeds the same `useAudioCapture` → WebSocket → `ASRProvider`
246: path. No changes to ASR, translation, VAD-interpretation, or refinement layers
247: are expected.
248: 
249: ## 9. Latency budget (target, for tuning once implemented)
250: 
251: | Stage | Target |
252: |---|---|
253: | Client capture → WS send | < 20 ms |
254: | ASR partial result | < 300 ms |
255: | Translation (cloud) | < 150 ms |
256: | Total: speech → on-screen translation | < 500 ms |
257: | LLM refinement (async, non-blocking) | 1–3 s, off critical path |
258: 
259: These are targets to validate against once providers are implemented, not
260: measured results.

(End of file - total 260 lines)
</content>

1: import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react"
2: 
3: export interface UseAudioCaptureOptions {
4:   simulate?: boolean
5:   onChunk?: (bytes: Uint8Array) => void
6:   sampleRate?: number
7: }
8: 
9: function resampleToPcm16(
10:   input: Float32Array,
11:   inputRate: number,
12:   outputRate: number,
13: ): Uint8Array {
14:   const ratio = inputRate / outputRate
15:   const outputLength = Math.max(1, Math.round(input.length / ratio))
16:   const pcm = new Int16Array(outputLength)
17:   for (let i = 0; i < outputLength; i += 1) {
18:     const index = Math.min(input.length - 1, Math.floor(i * ratio))
19:     let sample = input[index]
20:     if (sample > 1) sample = 1
21:     else if (sample < -1) sample = -1
22:     pcm[i] = sample < 0 ? sample * 0x8000 : sample * 0x7fff
23:   }
24:   return new Uint8Array(pcm.buffer)
25: }
26: 
27: export function useAudioCapture({
28:   simulate = false,
29:   onChunk,
30:   sampleRate = 16_000,
31: }: UseAudioCaptureOptions = {}) {
32:   const [stream, setStream] = useState<MediaStream | null>(null)
33:   const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null)
34:   const [isCapturing, setIsCapturing] = useState(false)
35:   const streamRef = useRef<MediaStream | null>(null)
36:   const simulateRef = useRef(simulate)
37:   simulateRef.current = simulate
38:   const onChunkRef = useRef(onChunk)
39:   onChunkRef.current = onChunk
40:   const sampleRateRef = useRef(sampleRate)
41:   sampleRateRef.current = sampleRate
42:   const audioContextRef = useRef<AudioContext | null>(null)
43:   const sourceNodeRef = useRef<MediaStreamAudioSourceNode | null>(null)
44:   const processorRef = useRef<ScriptProcessorNode | null>(null)
45: 
46:   const cleanupNodes = useCallback(() => {
47:     processorRef.current?.disconnect()
48:     sourceNodeRef.current?.disconnect()
49:     if (audioContextRef.current) {
50:       void audioContextRef.current.close()
51:     }
52:     processorRef.current = null
53:     sourceNodeRef.current = null
54:     audioContextRef.current = null
55:   }, [])
56: 
57:   const start = useCallback(async (): Promise<boolean> => {
58:     setError(null)
59:     if (simulateRef.current) {
60:       setIsCapturing(true)
61:       return true
62:     }
63:     try {
64:       const mediaStream = await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({
65:         audio: {
66:           channelCount: 1,
67:           echoCancellation: true,
68:           noiseSuppression: true,
69:         },
70:       })
71:       streamRef.current = mediaStream
72:       setStream(mediaStream)
73: 
74:       const contextCtor =
75:         window.AudioContext ??
76:         (window as unknown as { webkitAudioContext: typeof AudioContext }).webkitAudioContext
77:       const audioContext = new contextCtor()
78:       audioContextRef.current = audioContext
79:       sourceNodeRef.current = audioContext.createMediaStreamSource(mediaStream)
80: 
81:       const processor = audioContext.createScriptProcessor(4096, 1, 1)
82:       processorRef.current = processor
83:       const mutedGain = audioContext.createGain()
84:       mutedGain.gain.value = 0
85: 
86:       sourceNodeRef.current.connect(processor)
87:       processor.connect(mutedGain)
88:       mutedGain.connect(audioContext.destination)
89: 
90:       processor.onaudioprocess = (event: AudioProcessingEvent) => {
91:         const channel = event.inputBuffer.getChannelData(0)
92:         const bytes = resampleToPcm16(channel, audioContext.sampleRate, sampleRateRef.current)
93:         onChunkRef.current?.(bytes)
94:       }
95: 
96:       setIsCapturing(true)
97:       return true
98:     } catch (cause) {
99:       cleanupNodes()
100:       streamRef.current?.getTracks().forEach((track) => track.stop())
101:       streamRef.current = null
102:       setStream(null)
103:       setError(cause instanceof Error ? cause.message : "Unable to access the microphone")
104:       return false
105:     }
106:   }, [cleanupNodes])
107: 
108:   const stop = useCallback(() => {
109:     cleanupNodes()
110:     streamRef.current?.getTracks().forEach((track) => track.stop())
111:     streamRef.current = null
112:     setStream(null)
113:     setIsCapturing(false)
114:   }, [cleanupNodes])
115: 
116:   useEffect(
117:     () => () => {
118:       cleanupNodes()
119:       streamRef.current?.getTracks().forEach((track) => track.stop())
120:     },
121:     [cleanupNodes],
122:   )
123: 
124:   return { stream, error, isCapturing, start, stop }
125: }

1: import type {

8: 
9: const WS_PATH = "/ws/translate"
10: const MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS = 5
11: const RECONNECT_BASE_DELAY_MS = 500
12: 
13: function wsUrl(): string {
14:   const host = import.meta.env.VITE_BACKEND_HOST ?? "localhost:8000"
15:   const useTls = import.meta.env.VITE_BACKEND_USE_TLS === "true"
16:   const scheme = useTls ? "wss" : "ws"
17:   return `${scheme}://${host}${WS_PATH}`
18: }
19: 
20: export class TranslatorClient implements StreamingClient {
21:   private socket: WebSocket | null = null
22:   private pending: ClientMessage[] = []
23:   private explicitlyClosed = false
24:   private reconnectAttempts = 0
25:   private reconnectTimer: number | null = null
26:   private startSessionId: string | null = null
27:   private configuration: SessionConfiguration | null = null
28: 
29:   constructor(private readonly handlers: StreamingClientHandlers) {}
30: 
31:   get isOpen(): boolean {
32:     return this.socket?.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN
33:   }
34: 
35:   connect(): void {
36:     if (this.socket) return
37:     this.explicitlyClosed = false
38:     this.setState("connecting")
39:     this.openSocket()
40:   }
41: 
42:   sendStartSession(sessionId: string): void {
43:     this.startSessionId = sessionId
44:     this.queue({ type: "start_session", session_id: sessionId })
45:   }
46: 
47:   sendConfiguration(config: SessionConfiguration): void {
48:     this.configuration = config
49:     this.queue({ type: "session_configuration", ...config })
50:   }
51: 
52:   sendAudio(bytes: Uint8Array): void {
53:     if (this.socket?.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) {
54:       this.socket.send(bytes)
55:     }
56:   }
57: 
58:   sendStopSession(sessionId: string): void {
59:     this.queue({ type: "stop_session", session_id: sessionId })
60:   }
61: 
62:   close(): void {
63:     this.explicitlyClosed = true
64:     this.stopReconnect()
65:     this.pending = []
66:     if (this.socket) {
67:       this.socket.onclose = null
68:       this.socket.close()
69:       this.socket = null
70:     }
71:     this.setState("idle")
72:   }
73: 
74:   private openSocket(): void {
75:     const socket = new WebSocket(wsUrl())
76:     this.socket = socket
77:     socket.binaryType = "arraybuffer"
78: 
79:     socket.onopen = () => {
80:       this.reconnectAttempts = 0
81:       if (this.startSessionId) {
82:         this.pending.unshift({ type: "start_session", session_id: this.startSessionId })
83:       }
84:       if (this.configuration) {
85:         this.pending.push({ type: "session_configuration", ...this.configuration })
86:       }
87:       this.flushQueue()
88:       this.setState("connected")
89:     }
90: 
91:     socket.onmessage = (event: MessageEvent) => {
92:       if (typeof event.data !== "string") return
93:       try {
94:         const data = JSON.parse(event.data) as ServerEvent
95:         this.handlers.onEvent(data)
96:       } catch {
97:         this.handlers.onError("Received a malformed message from the server")
98:       }
99:     }
100: 
101:     socket.onerror = () => {
102:       this.handlers.onError("WebSocket connection error")
103:     }
104: 
105:     socket.onclose = () => {
106:       if (this.socket !== socket) return
107:       this.socket = null
108:       if (this.explicitlyClosed) {
109:         this.setState("disconnected")
110:         return
111:       }
112:       this.scheduleReconnect()
113:     }
114:   }
115: 
116:   private queue(message: ClientMessage): void {
117:     if (this.socket?.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) {
118:       this.sendJson(message)
119:       return
120:     }
121:     this.pending.push(message)
122:   }
123: 
124:   private flushQueue(): void {
125:     const messages = this.pending
126:     this.pending = []
127:     for (const message of messages) {
128:       this.sendJson(message)
129:     }
130:   }
131: 
132:   private scheduleReconnect(): void {
133:     if (this.explicitlyClosed) return
134:     if (this.reconnectAttempts >= MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS) {
135:       this.setState("disconnected")
136:       this.handlers.onError("Connection lost. Reconnect attempts exhausted.")
137:       return
138:     }
139:     this.setState("reconnecting")
140:     const delay = RECONNECT_BASE_DELAY_MS * 2 ** this.reconnectAttempts
141:     this.reconnectAttempts += 1
142:     this.reconnectTimer = window.setTimeout(() => {
143:       this.reconnectTimer = null
144:       if (this.explicitlyClosed) return
145:       this.setState("reconnecting")
146:       this.openSocket()
147:     }, delay)
148:   }
149: 
150:   private stopReconnect(): void {
151:     if (this.reconnectTimer !== null) {
152:       window.clearTimeout(this.reconnectTimer)
153:       this.reconnectTimer = null
154:     }
155:   }
156: 
157:   private sendJson(payload: ClientMessage): void {
158:     if (this.socket?.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) {
159:       this.socket.send(JSON.stringify(payload))
160:     }
161:   }
162: 
163:   private setState(state: ConnectionState): void {
164:     this.handlers.onStateChange(state)
165:   }
166: }

178:     this.setConnectionState("reconnecting")
179:     await this.sleep(1500)
180:     if (this.stopped) return
181:     this.setConnectionState("connected")
182:     this.emitSessionStarted()
183:   }
184: 
185:   private emit(event: ServerEvent): void {
186:     this.handlers.onEvent(event)
187:   }
188: 
189:   private emitSessionStarted(): void {
190:     this.emit({
191:       type: "session_started",
192:       session_id: this.sessionId,
193:       configuration: {
194:         ...this.configuration,
195:         session_id: this.sessionId,
196:       },
197:     })
198:   }
199: 
200:   private emitTranscript(
201:     segmentId: string,
202:     text: string,
203:     isFinal: boolean,
204:   ): void {
205:     this.emit({
206:       type: isFinal ? "final_transcript" : "partial_transcript",
207:       session_id: this.sessionId,
208:       segment_id: segmentId,
209:       text,
210:       is_final: isFinal,
211:     })
212:   }
213: 
214:   private emitTranslation(
215:     segmentId: string,
216:     sourceText: string,
217:     translatedText: string,
218:   ): void {
219:     this.emit({
220:       type: "translation",
221:       session_id: this.sessionId,
222:       segment_id: segmentId,
223:       source_text: sourceText,
224:       translated_text: translatedText,
225:       source_language: this.configuration.source_language,
226:       target_language: this.configuration.target_language,
227:       is_final: true,
228:       provider: "mock",
229:     })
230:   }
231: 
232:   private emitLatency(segmentId: string): void {
233:     const jitter = Math.floor(Math.random() * 80)
234:     this.emit({
235:       type: "latency",
236:       session_id: this.sessionId,
237:       segment_id: segmentId,
238:       asr_ms: 180 + jitter,
239:       translation_ms: 110 + jitter / 2,
240:       end_to_end_ms: 290 + jitter,
241:     })
242:   }
243: 
244:   private setConnectionState(state: ConnectionState): void {
245:     this.handlers.onStateChange(state)
246:   }
247: 
248:   private sleep(ms: number): Promise<void> {
249:     return new Promise((resolve) => {
250:       this.pendingSleep = resolve
251:       const id = window.setTimeout(() => {
252:         this.pendingSleep = null
253:         resolve()
254:       }, ms)
255:       this.timers.add(id)
256:     })
257:   }
258: 
259:   private schedule(fn: () => void, ms: number): void {
260:     const id = window.setTimeout(() => {
261:       this.timers.delete(id)
262:       fn()
263:     }, ms)
264:     this.timers.add(id)
265:   }

1: """
2: WebSocket endpoint for the live audio -> transcript -> translation pipeline.
3: 
4: The transport layer owns the connection: it accepts sockets, validates and
5: routes client control messages, and manages per-session lifecycle. Because no
6: real ASR/translation provider is wired in yet, each session drives the
7: deterministic `SimulatedTranscript` (see app/services/simulation.py) so the
8: full browser -> backend -> browser event loop is observable end to end. The
9: event loop is never blocked: audio handling is O(1) bookkeeping, silence
10: detection runs on a per-session asyncio task, and every network write is
11: guarded by a per-session lock.
12: """

14: 
15: import asyncio
16: import json
17: import time
18: import uuid

39: class Session:

42:     def __init__(self, session_id: str, websocket: WebSocket, settings: Settings) -> None:

45:         self.settings = settings
46:         self.config: schemas.SessionConfiguration | None = None
47:         self.simulator = SimulatedTranscript()
48:         self.state = "created"
49:         self.received_chunks = 0
50:         self.received_bytes = 0
51:         self.audio_seconds = 0.0
52:         self.last_audio_at = 0.0
53:         self.segment_id: str | None = None
54:         self.segment_start_ms: int | None = None
55:         self.segment_start_monotonic = 0.0
56:         self.segment_audio_seconds = 0.0
57:         self.bytes_per_second = 32000.0
58:         self._segment_counter = 0
59:         self._last_partial = ""
60:         self._send_lock = asyncio.Lock()
61:         self.monitor_task: asyncio.Task | None = None
62: 
63:     @property
64:     def configured(self) -> bool:
65:         return self.config is not None
66: 
67:     async def apply_config(self, config: schemas.SessionConfiguration) -> None:
68:         self.config = config
69:         self.state = "configured"
70:         self.bytes_per_second = self._bytes_per_second(config)
71:         if self.monitor_task is None or self.monitor_task.done():
72:             self.monitor_task = asyncio.create_task(self._silence_monitor())
73: 
74:     async def receive_audio(self, chunk: bytes) -> None:
75:         if not self.configured:
76:             await self._send_error("no_active_session", "Configure a session before sending audio")
77:             return
78:         now = time.monotonic()
79:         self.received_chunks += 1
80:         self.received_bytes += len(chunk)
81:         self.audio_seconds += len(chunk) / self.bytes_per_second
82:         self.last_audio_at = now
83: 
84:         if self.state == "speaking":
85:             self.segment_audio_seconds += len(chunk) / self.bytes_per_second
86:             await self._emit_partial()
87:             return
88: 
89:         if self.state == "silence":
90:             self.state = "speaking"
91:             self._begin_segment(now)
92:             await self.send_event(

95:                     session_id=self.session_id,
96:                     timestamp_ms=_now_ms(),
97:                 )
98:             )
99:             await self._emit_partial()
100:             return
101: 
102:         self.state = "speaking"
103:         self._begin_segment(now)
104:         await self.send_event(
105:             schemas.SpeechEvent(

107:                 session_id=self.session_id,
108:                 timestamp_ms=_now_ms(),

112: 
113:     async def finalize_on_silence(self, now: float) -> None:
114:         if self.state != "speaking":

118:         await self.send_event(

124:             )
125:         )
126:         await self._emit_finalized_segment(now)
127: 
128:     async def stop(self, reason: str) -> None:

132:         await self.send_event(
133:             schemas.SessionStoppedEvent(session_id=self.session_id, reason=reason)
134:         )
135:         await self._teardown()
136: 
137:     async def _teardown(self) -> None:
138:         if self.monitor_task is not None:
139:             self.monitor_task.cancel()
140:             try:
141:                 await self.monitor_task
142:             except asyncio.CancelledError:
143:                 pass

146:     def _begin_segment(self, now: float) -> None:

148:         self._segment_counter += 1

150:         self.segment_start_monotonic = now

152:         self.segment_audio_seconds = 0.0
153:         self._last_partial = ""
154: 
155:     async def _emit_partial(self) -> None:
156:         if self.segment_id is None:
157:             return
158:         text = self.simulator.partial_for(self.segment_audio_seconds)
159:         if text and text != self._last_partial:
160:             self._last_partial = text
161:             await self.send_event(
162:                 schemas.TranscriptEvent(

166:                     text=text,
167:                     is_final=False,
168:                     start_ms=self.segment_start_ms,
169:                 )
170:             )
171: 
172:     async def _emit_finalized_segment(self, now: float) -> None:
173:         if self.segment_id is None or self.config is None:
174:             self.segment_id = None
175:             return
176:         segment_id = self.segment_id
177:         text = self.simulator.current_text
178:         end_ms = _now_ms()
179:         await self.send_event(
180:             schemas.TranscriptEvent(
181:                 type="final_transcript",

183:                 segment_id=segment_id,
184:                 text=text,
185:                 is_final=True,
186:                 start_ms=self.segment_start_ms,
187:                 end_ms=end_ms,
188:                 confidence=0.95,
189:             )
190:         )
191:         await self.send_event(
192:             schemas.TranslationEvent(
193:                 session_id=self.session_id,
194:                 segment_id=segment_id,
195:                 source_text=text,
196:                 translated_text=self.simulator.translated(self.config.target_language),
197:                 source_language=self.config.source_language,
198:                 target_language=self.config.target_language,
199:                 is_final=True,
200:                 provider="simulated",
201:             )
202:         )
203:         refined_text, changed = self.simulator.refined()
204:         await self.send_event(
205:             schemas.RefinedTranscriptEvent(

207:                 segment_id=segment_id,
208:                 refined_text=refined_text,
209:                 changed=changed,
210:             )
211:         )
212:         await self.send_event(
213:             schemas.LatencyEvent(
214:                 session_id=self.session_id,
215:                 segment_id=segment_id,
216:                 asr_ms=180.0,
217:                 translation_ms=120.0,
218:                 end_to_end_ms=round((now - self.segment_start_monotonic) * 1000, 1),
219:             )
220:         )
221:         self.segment_id = None
222: 
223:     async def _silence_monitor(self) -> None:
224:         try:
225:             while True:
226:                 await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
227:                 if self.state != "speaking":
228:                     continue
229:                 now = time.monotonic()
230:                 silent_ms = (now - self.last_audio_at) * 1000
231:                 if silent_ms >= self.settings.silence_finalize_ms:
232:                     await self.finalize_on_silence(now)
233:         except asyncio.CancelledError:

235: 
236:     async def send_event(self, event: schemas.ServerEvent) -> None:
237:         async with self._send_lock:

240:             except Exception:

258: class SessionManager:

409:         return current

417:         return await _handle_start_session(websocket, payload, current)
418:     if message_type == schemas.WSClientEventType.SESSION_CONFIGURATION.value:
419:         return await _handle_configuration(websocket, payload, current)

422:         return current
423:     if message_type == schemas.WSClientEventType.STOP_SESSION.value:
424:         return await _handle_stop_session(websocket, payload, current)

430: @router.websocket("/translate")
431: async def translate_stream(websocket: WebSocket) -> None:
432:     """
433:     Protocol (see app/models/schemas.py for exact payloads):
434:       Client -> Server:
435:         - JSON {"type": "start_session", "session_id"?: str}
436:         - JSON {"type": "session_configuration", ...SessionConfiguration}
437:         - binary frames: raw PCM16/Opus audio chunks
438:         - JSON {"type": "audio_chunk", "session_id": str} (control, optional)
439:         - JSON {"type": "stop_session", "session_id": str}
440:       Server -> Client (all JSON envelopes):
441:         - session_started / speech_started / partial_transcript / final_transcript
442:         - silence_detected / speech_resumed / translation / refined_transcript
443:         - latency / error / session_stopped
444:     """
445:     await websocket.accept()
446:     session: Session | None = None
447:     logger.info("ws_connected", websocket=id(websocket))
448: 
449:     try:
450:         while True:
451:             message = await websocket.receive()
452: 
453:             if message.get("type") == "websocket.disconnect":
454:                 break
455: 
456:             if "text" in message and message["text"] is not None:
457:                 session = await _handle_text_message(websocket, message["text"], session)
458:                 continue
459: 
460:             if "bytes" in message and message["bytes"] is not None:
461:                 chunk = message["bytes"]
462:                 if len(chunk) > get_settings().max_ws_message_bytes:

1: """
2: Shared Pydantic models for the WebSocket translation protocol.
3: 
4: The client/server contract lives here so the WebSocket transport layer and
5: any future pipeline orchestrator speak the same vocabulary. Every message is
6: a JSON envelope of the form ``{"type": "<event>", ...fields}``; audio frames
7: travel as raw binary WebSocket messages rather than base64-encoded JSON.
8: """
9: from __future__ import annotations
10: 
11: from enum import Enum
12: from typing import Literal
13: 
14: from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
15: 
16: AudioEncoding = Literal["linear16", "opus"]
17: 
18: 
19: class WSClientEventType(str, Enum):
20:     """Messages the frontend sends to the backend."""
21: 
22:     START_SESSION = "start_session"
23:     SESSION_CONFIGURATION = "session_configuration"
24:     AUDIO_CHUNK = "audio_chunk"
25:     STOP_SESSION = "stop_session"
26: 
27: 
28: class WSServerEventType(str, Enum):
29:     """Messages the backend sends to the frontend."""
30: 
31:     SESSION_STARTED = "session_started"
32:     PARTIAL_TRANSCRIPT = "partial_transcript"
33:     FINAL_TRANSCRIPT = "final_transcript"
34:     SPEECH_STARTED = "speech_started"
35:     SILENCE_DETECTED = "silence_detected"
36:     SPEECH_RESUMED = "speech_resumed"
37:     TRANSLATION = "translation"
38:     REFINED_TRANSCRIPT = "refined_transcript"
39:     LATENCY = "latency"
40:     ERROR = "error"
41:     SESSION_STOPPED = "session_stopped"
42: 
43: 
44: # --- Client -> Server -------------------------------------------------------
45: 
46: 
47: class StartSessionRequest(BaseModel):
48:     """Ask the server to begin a translation session for this connection."""
49: 
50:     session_id: str | None = Field(
51:         default=None,
52:         description="Client-generated UUID. The server generates one when omitted.",
53:     )
54: 
55: 
56: class SessionConfiguration(BaseModel):
57:     """Full configuration for a session: languages, audio source, session id."""
58: 
59:     session_id: str
60:     source_language: str = Field(description="BCP-47 code, e.g. 'en', or 'auto'")
61:     target_language: str = Field(description="BCP-47 code, e.g. 'es'")
62:     audio_source: str = Field(description="'microphone', 'system', or a mock source id")
63:     sample_rate: int = 16_000
64:     encoding: AudioEncoding = "linear16"
65: 
66: 
67: class AudioChunkMessage(BaseModel):
68:     """Optional JSON control message around binary audio frames."""
69: 
70:     session_id: str
71: 
72: 
73: class StopSessionRequest(BaseModel):
74:     """Gracefully end a session."""
75: 
76:     session_id: str
77: 
78: 
79: # --- Server -> Client -------------------------------------------------------
80: 
81: 
82: class SessionStartedEvent(BaseModel):
83:     """Emitted when a session exists with a known configuration."""
84: 
85:     type: Literal["session_started"] = "session_started"
86:     session_id: str
87:     configuration: SessionConfiguration
88: 
89: 
90: class SpeechEvent(BaseModel):
91:     """speech_started / silence_detected / speech_resumed lifecycle events."""
92: 
93:     type: Literal["speech_started", "silence_detected", "speech_resumed"]
94:     session_id: str
95:     timestamp_ms: int
96:     duration_ms: int | None = None  # silence_detected only: how long the gap was
97: 
98: 
99: class TranscriptEvent(BaseModel):
100:     """partial_transcript / final_transcript streamed ASR results."""
101: 
102:     type: Literal["partial_transcript", "final_transcript"]
103:     session_id: str
104:     segment_id: str
105:     text: str
106:     is_final: bool
107:     start_ms: int | None = None
108:     end_ms: int | None = None
109:     confidence: float | None = None
110: 
111: 
112: class TranslationEvent(BaseModel):
113:     """A translation of a finalized transcript segment."""
114: 
115:     type: Literal["translation"] = "translation"
116:     session_id: str
117:     segment_id: str
118:     source_text: str
119:     translated_text: str
120:     source_language: str
121:     target_language: str
122:     is_final: bool = True
123:     provider: str
124: 
125: 
126: class RefinedTranscriptEvent(BaseModel):
127:     """Async, non-blocking correction of an already-finalized segment."""
128: 
129:     type: Literal["refined_transcript"] = "refined_transcript"
130:     session_id: str
131:     segment_id: str
132:     refined_text: str
133:     changed: bool
134: 
135: 
136: class LatencyEvent(BaseModel):
137:     """Per-segment timing report (ms)."""
138: 
139:     type: Literal["latency"] = "latency"
140:     session_id: str
141:     segment_id: str
142:     asr_ms: float | None = None
143:     translation_ms: float | None = None
144:     end_to_end_ms: float | None = None
145: 
146: 
147: class ErrorMessage(BaseModel):
148:     """Error envelope sent to the client."""
149: 
150:     type: Literal["error"] = "error"
151:     session_id: str | None = None
152:     code: str

154: 
155: 
156: class SessionStoppedEvent(BaseModel):

158: 
159:     type: Literal["session_stopped"] = "session_stopped"
160:     session_id: str
161:     reason: str
162: 
163: 
164: # --- Internal pipeline data models (used by provider interfaces) -----------

166:

174: 
175:

179:     translated_text: str
180:     source_language: str
181:     target_language: str
182:     is_final: bool
183:     provider: str
184: 
185: 
186: class RefinementResult(BaseModel):
187:     segment_id: str
188:     refined_text: str
189:     changed: bool
190: 
191: 
192: ServerEvent = (
193:     SessionStartedEvent
194:     | SpeechEvent
195:     | TranscriptEvent
196:     | TranslationEvent
197:     | RefinedTranscriptEvent
198:     | LatencyEvent
199:     | ErrorMessage
200:     | SessionStoppedEvent
201: )

115: ## Design principles
116: 
117: 1. **Provider abstractions everywhere.** `ASRProvider`, `TranslationProvider`,
118:    `LLMProvider`, and a client-side `VADProvider` mean no business logic is
119:    tightly coupled to Deepgram, a specific translation API, or a specific LLM.
120: 2. **Latency-critical path stays lean.** ASR → translation → display is the hot
121:    path. LLM refinement is strictly async and only ever *improves* text already
122:    shown to the user — it never blocks it.
123: 3. **Silence is signal.** Client-side VAD silence events double as endpointing
124:    hints, giving cleaner sentence boundaries and punctuation than relying on
125:    ASR endpointing alone.
126: 4. **UI needs no manual.** Two panels (original / translation), one big
127:    start/stop control, obvious connection and latency indicators.
128: 
129: ## Roadmap
130: 
131: See `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md` for the phased plan, from this scaffold through
132: production hardening and system/meeting-audio ingestion.

### Worklet file details

```ts
// src/audio/pcmCaptureWorklet.ts

declare const sampleRate: number
declare function registerProcessor(name: string, processor: new () => AudioWorkletProcessor): void

interface CaptureConfig {
  type: "configure"
  outputSampleRate: number
  chunkSamples: number
  speechThreshold: number
  hangoverMs: number
}

class PcmCaptureProcessor extends AudioWorkletProcessor {
  private queue: number[] = []
  private frac0 = 0
  private ratio = 1
  private outputSampleRate = 16000
  private chunkSamples = 1600
  private speechThreshold = 0.01
  private hangoverS = 0.3
  private speaking = false
  private hangoverRemaining = 0

  constructor() {
    super()
    this.port.onmessage = (event: MessageEvent<CaptureConfig>) => {
      const message = event.data
      if (message?.type !== "configure") return
      this.outputSampleRate = message.outputSampleRate
      this.chunkSamples = message.chunkSamples
      this.speechThreshold = message.speechThreshold
      this.hangoverS = message.hangoverMs / 1000
      this.ratio = sampleRate / this.outputSampleRate
      this.frac0 = 0
    }
  }

  process(inputs: Float32Array[][], _outputs: Float32Array[][]) {
    const input = inputs[0]?.[0]
    if (!input || input.length === 0) return true

    this.pushResampled(input)

    if (this.queue.length >= this.chunkSamples) {
      const samples = this.queue.splice(0, this.chunkSamples)
      const pcm = new Int16Array(samples.length)
      for (let i = 0; i < samples.length; i++) {
        let s = samples[i]
        if (s > 1) s = 1
        else if (s < -1) s = -1
        pcm[i] = s < 0 ? s * 0x8000 : s * 0x7fff
      }
      this.port.postMessage({ type: "audio", buffer: pcm.buffer }, [pcm.buffer])
    }

    this.updateActivity(input)
    return true
  }

  private pushResampled(input: Float32Array) {
    const length = input.length
    if (length === 0) return
    let p = this.frac0
    const last = length - 1
    while (p <= last) {
      const i0 = Math.floor(p)
      const i1 = i0 < last ? i0 + 1 : last
      const f = p - i0
      this.queue.push(input[i0] * (1 - f) + input[i1] * f)
      p += this.ratio
    }
    this.frac0 = p - last
  }

  private updateActivity(input: Float32Array) {
    let sum = 0
    for (let i = 0; i < input.length; i++) {
      const s = input[i]
      sum += s * s
    }
    const rms = Math.sqrt(sum / input.length)
    const quantumS = input.length / sampleRate

    if (rms >= this.speechThreshold) {
      this.hangoverRemaining = this.hangoverS
      if (!this.speaking) {
        this.speaking = true
        this.port.postMessage({ type: "activity", active: true })
      }
    } else if (this.speaking) {
      this.hangoverRemaining -= quantumS
      if (this.hangoverRemaining <= 0) {
        this.speaking = false
        this.port.postMessage({ type: "activity", active: false })
      }
    }
  }
}

registerProcessor("pcm-capture-processor", PcmCaptureProcessor)
```

```python
class Session:
    def __init__(self, session_id, websocket, settings):
        self.session_id = session_id
        self.websocket = websocket
        self.settings = settings
        self.config = None
        self.state = "created"
        self.received_chunks = 0
        self.received_bytes = 0
        self.audio_seconds = 0.0
        self.last_audio_at = 0.0
        self.last_ack_at = 0.0
        self.bytes_per_second = 32000.0
        self._send_lock = asyncio.Lock()

    @property
    def configured(self): ...

    async def apply_config(self, config):
        self.config = config
        self.state = "configured"
        self.bytes_per_second = self._bytes_per_second(config)

    async def receive_audio(self, chunk: bytes):
        if not self.configured:
            await self._send_error("no_active_session", "Configure a session before sending audio")
            return
        now = time.monotonic()
        self.received_chunks += 1
        self.received_bytes += len(chunk)
        self.audio_seconds += len(chunk) / self.bytes_per_second
        self.last_audio_at = now
        if now - self.last_ack_at >= _AUDIO_ACK_INTERVAL_MS / 1000:
            self.last_ack_at = now
            await self.send_event(schemas.AudioReceivedEvent(...))
            logger.info("audio_received", session_id=..., chunks=..., bytes=..., audio_seconds=...)

    async def stop(self, reason):
        if self.state == "stopped": return
        self.state = "stopped"
        await self.send_event(schemas.SessionStoppedEvent(...))
```

```ts
export class MockStreamingClient implements StreamingClient {
  private readonly handlers: StreamingClientHandlers
  private timers = new Set<number>()
  private stopped = true
  private sessionId = "mock-session"
  private configuration: SessionConfiguration = DEFAULT_CONFIGURATION

  constructor(handlers) { this.handlers = handlers }

  get isOpen() { return !this.stopped }

  connect(): void {
    if (!this.stopped) return
    this.stopped = false
    this.handlers.onStateChange("connecting")
    const id = window.setTimeout(() => {
      this.timers.delete(id)
      if (this.stopped) return
      this.handlers.onStateChange("connected")
      this.handlers.onEvent({
        type: "session_started",
        session_id: this.sessionId,
        configuration: { ...this.configuration, session_id: this.sessionId },
      })
    }, 300)
    this.timers.add(id)
  }

  sendStartSession(sessionId) { this.sessionId = sessionId }
  sendConfiguration(config) { this.configuration = { ...this.configuration, ...config } }
  sendAudio(_bytes) {}
  sendStopSession(_sessionId) {}
  close() {
    this.stopped = true
    this.timers.forEach((id) => window.clearTimeout(id))
    this.timers.clear()
  }
}
```

  chunksPerSecond: number

}

export function useAudioCapture({
  simulate = false,
  onChunk,
  targetSampleRate = 16_000,
  chunkSizeMs = 100,
}: UseAudioCaptureOptions = {}) {
  const [stream, setStream] = useState<MediaStream | null>(null)
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null)
  const [isCapturing, setIsCapturing] = useState(false)
  const [isSpeaking, setIsSpeaking] = useState(false)
  const [activityAvailable, setActivityAvailable] = useState(false)
  const [sampleRate, setSampleRate] = useState<number | null>(null)
  const [chunkSizeBytes, setChunkSizeBytes] = useState(2 * Math.round(targetSampleRate * chunkSizeMs / 1000))
  const [chunksPerSecond, setChunksPerSecond] = useState(0)
  const [bytesSent, setBytesSent] = useState(0)

  const streamRef = useRef<MediaStream | null>(null)
  const audioContextRef = useRef<AudioContext | null>(null)
  const sourceNodeRef = useRef<MediaStreamAudioSourceNode | null>(null)
  const workletNodeRef = useRef<AudioWorkletNode | null>(null)
  const muteGainRef = useRef<GainNode | null>(null)
  const capturingRef = useRef(false)
  const simulateRef = useRef(simulate)
  simulateRef.current = simulate
  const onChunkRef = useRef(onChunk)
  onChunkRef.current = onChunk
  const targetSampleRateRef = useRef(targetSampleRate)
  targetSampleRateRef.current = targetSampleRate
  const chunkSizeMsRef = useRef(chunkSizeMs)
  chunkSizeMsRef.current = chunkSizeMs
  const chunksRef = useRef(0)
  const bytesSentRef = useRef(0)
  const statsTimerRef = useRef<number | null>(null)
  const lastStatsCountRef = useRef(0)

  const teardown = useCallback((updateState: boolean) => {
    if (statsTimerRef.current !== null) {
      window.clearInterval(statsTimerRef.current)
      statsTimerRef.current = null
    }
    workletNodeRef.current?.port.onmessage = null
    workletNodeRef.current?.port.close()
    workletNodeRef.current?.disconnect()
    workletNodeRef.current = null
    sourceNodeRef.current?.disconnect()
    sourceNodeRef.current = null
    muteGainRef.current?.disconnect()
    muteGainRef.current = null
    const ctx = audioContextRef.current
    audioContextRef.current = null
    if (ctx) {
      void ctx.close().catch(() => undefined)
    }
    streamRef.current?.getTracks().forEach((track) => track.stop())
    streamRef.current = null
    capturingRef.current = false
    chunksRef.current = 0
    bytesSentRef.current = 0
    lastStatsCountRef.current = 0
    setChunksPerSecond(0)
    setBytesSent(0)
    setIsSpeaking(false)
    setActivityAvailable(false)
    setSampleRate(null)
    if (updateState) {
      setStream(null)
      setIsCapturing(false)
    }
  }, [])
  ...
}
